Helio Start Field-Handling Quick Reference
============================================

Five readiness fields stay distinct. A YES on one does not clear, modify, or
substitute another. Each carries its own state independently.

Readiness fields (must remain separate)
---------------------------------------
- Helio admin proof — qualifying human admin present and current.
- Supported billing — billing conditions supported.
- Connector authentication — selected connector authenticated.
- External-system authority — owner-level permission or network-allowlist
  action verified (or unavailable owner identified).
- Customer Success work state — no active CS adoption or renewal work
  suppressing the lifecycle path.

Rule
----
External authority is a separate readiness input from admin proof and
connector authentication. Pending external authority blocks setup
messaging even when the other fields are YES.

External-authority field ownership
----------------------------------
- Records the external-authority state: Daniela. She holds the schema
  field parallel to connector_authentication; values are verified or
  pending, and the field stays distinct from admin proof and connector
  authentication.
- Withholds setup messaging while external authority is pending: Ines.
  She owns lifecycle copy; held prompts release only after CS verifies
  the authority record and Daniela flips the field to verified.
- Reports external-authority status separately: Owen. Checklist
  exposure stays distinct from admission and activation outcomes and is
  not folded into admin proof, connector authentication, entitlement,
  billing, or deployment.

Routing on state
----------------
- external_authority = verified → continue. Admin proof, connector
  authentication, entitlement, billing, and deployment remain
  independent gates.
- external_authority = pending → route to Customer Success; setup
  prompts held; workspace not admitted.

What this is not
----------------
Not a launch, GA expansion, paid-acquisition claim, or transfer of CS
authority. External-authority verified is not the same as launched,
paid, mature, or retained.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
CS AUTO-NUDGE MESSAGING-STATE REVIEW
Current Authority Reference
Effective 2028-01-01
═══════════════════════════════════════════════

BASIS

    - Five governed meanings contract (external-system authority,
      connector authentication, entitlement, qualifying-human-admin
      status, active CS adoption/renewal work).
    - External-system authority definition: connector readiness, NOT
      contact permission.


──────────────────────────────────────────────
1. WHEN INES MAY CLOSE A REVIEW
   (no line-by-line Riley approval required)
──────────────────────────────────────────────

All of the following must hold:

    a. Surface is one of the four live consumers OR the fifth consumer
       operating under its accepted scope.
    b. All five governed fields are present, current, and consistent
       across reporting and lifecycle views.
    c. No semantic interpretation is disputed (freshness/agreement, not
       a meaning question).
    d. No proposed state-meaning change is in flight.
    e. No customer correction is required or implied — no message sent
       or queued against the row.
    f. No incident stop is in effect for the row or surface.
    g. No hold is active: every required field has cleared the
       missing / stale / unresolved / conflicting gate.
    h. The review is routine messaging-state consumption (not
       state-changing release, not release review, not mature-outcome
       packet assembly).
    i. No field self-certification in play (named-owner certification
       preserved where required: Daniela for source/connector, Ines for
       lifecycle state).

Closure requires a fresh reevaluation after any prior reconciliation;
views must be visibly current at close.


──────────────────────────────────────────────
2. ROUTINE OPERATOR GUIDANCE INES MAY OWN
   (no line-by-line Riley approval required)
──────────────────────────────────────────────

Ines may author, update, and present routine operator guidance when:

    a. Derived from the accepted Q3 guides and stays within their
       definitions.
    b. Five governed meanings stay separate and externally defined; no
       conflation (e.g., connector readiness vs contact permission).
    c. External-system authority stays scoped to connector readiness;
       not broadened to contact permission or other meanings.
    d. Hold contract named: missing/stale/unresolved/conflicting →
       field-specific hold on the affected nudge decision only.
    e. Operators do NOT manually release holds (stated explicitly).
    f. Four-consumer base preserved; fifth consumer stays under its
       accepted scope; no sixth consumer introduced.
    g. Lifecycle-surface behavior not redefined: other lifecycle
       surfaces consume shared state under their own consumer rules;
       the CS auto-nudge hold does not propagate.
    h. Routing boundaries preserved: state-meaning changes, disputed
       interpretations, customer corrections, incident stops → Riley;
       engineering release and rollback → Daniela.
    i. Walkthroughs, handouts, #customer-success posts stay within the
       above and do not imply broadened authority.

Two approved Q3 references = evidence Ines can carry the explanation.
They are not authorization for closure beyond what Section 1 states.


──────────────────────────────────────────────
3. WHAT MUST BE ESCALATED TO RILEY
──────────────────────────────────────────────

Escalate regardless of how routine the surface looks:

    a. Any proposed state-meaning change (any of the five governed
       meanings, or external-system authority scope).
    b. Any disputed interpretation of a governed field, even when views
       are currently fresh — semantic disagreement is not staleness.
    c. Any customer correction: message sent or queued against a row
       that should not have fired, or correction implied by a held row
       that previously went out.
    d. Any incident stop, including contained CS auto-nudge retries and
       worker-restart requeues.
    e. Cross-surface discrepancy where a held nudge decision touches
       another lifecycle surface.
    f. Authority-broadening requests — e.g., expanding reminder scope
       to any-logged-in-member, loosening qualifying-human-admin
       criteria, broadening external-system authority to contact
       permission.
    g. Adding a sixth consumer, or reclassifying the fifth consumer's
       scope.
    h. Reclassification of a routine review as non-routine, ambiguous,
       or exception-heavy.
    i. Source-age breach declarations or replay-control decisions.
    j. Any conflict where merge-alias or entitlement disagreement
       remains unresolved after engineering trace (Daniela traces
       source; Riley decides disposition).


──────────────────────────────────────────────
4. WORK OUTSIDE THIS AUTHORITY
──────────────────────────────────────────────

Remains outside Ines's lane regardless of routine appearance:

    a. Engineering release and rollback control — Daniela.
    b. New template, schema, field, or surface additions — Engineering
       + Riley.
    c. Lifecycle program policy changes (cadence, audience definition,
       suppression rules) — Riley.
    d. Source-age alert thresholds, breach declarations, evidence-
       ledger rule changes — Owen (ledger) + Riley jointly.
    e. Mature-outcome packet assembly for closed cohorts — Owen, with
       named-owner certification; no self-certification; descriptive
       coverage only.
    f. Operator manual override of a hold — prohibited. Only fresh
       reevaluation + reconciled views clear a hold.
    g. Modifying the five governed meanings — Riley.
    h. Changing the four-consumer base or fifth-consumer scope — Riley.
    i. Cross-consumer scope expansion toward a sixth consumer — Riley,
       declined by default per 2027-12-17.
    j. Authority decisions affecting Daniela's engineering control or
       Priya's review scope — out of band.


──────────────────────────────────────────────
HOLD CONTRACT (REFERENCE)
──────────────────────────────────────────────

    Trigger:  any required field is missing, stale (past freshness
              window), unresolved (e.g., conflicting merge-alias
              evidence), or conflicting (views disagree on semantic
              content).

    Effect:   visible field-specific hold on the affected nudge
              decision only. Other lifecycle surfaces continue under
              their own consumer rules.

    Release:  only by fresh reevaluation with reporting and lifecycle
              views reconciled. No manual override, no template
              substitution, no engineering force-release, no customer
              correction implied. A hold is a non-send state.


──────────────────────────────────────────────
BOUNDARY STATEMENT
──────────────────────────────────────────────

    This reference documents the existing routine lane as of 2028-01-01.
    It does not broaden Ines's review-closure authority, release
    authority, or operator-guidance scope. The two accepted Q3
    message-state guides remain independent evidence of her ability to
    carry the explanation; they are not authorization for closure beyond
    Section 1 above. The five governed meanings stay separate; external-
    system authority stays at connector readiness; engineering release
    and rollback stay with Daniela; the stop owner for state-meaning
    changes, disputed interpretations, customer corrections, and
    incident stops stays with Riley.

input.body:
Context. Mid-segment churn signal first surfaced at the February 9, 2023 staff review: 50–200 seat cut at 5.1% monthly churn against a 2.1% trailing-six-month baseline. Cohort-definition re-checked by Owen and not a cut bug. EXP-2023-02-onboarding-trigger (`lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2`) ran mid-March, cleared its second cohort at +3.1 pts pooled week-1 retention, and shipped at 100% on April 10, 2023 to mid-segment + growth tier (not starter).

State at the April 21, 2023 review.
- Two post-ship weekly cohorts observed: Apr 10 cohort +3.2 pts, Apr 17 cohort +1.4 pts vs baseline.
- Tomas Vega got the clean read; Marcus Vail moved to board-call timing rather than contesting the data.
- Three framings on the table; the investigation was explicitly NOT being closed.

Evidence still required before calling the issue fixed.
- A third complete post-ship weekly cohort — the cohort window was expected to land around April 24, 2023, i.e., the following week.
- Three post-ship weekly cohorts in aggregate, so the "is this variance or real" question stops being arguable either direction.
- Owen's mix-shift checks on the third cohort (signup source, tier, geo, day-of-week) to rule out composition rather than trigger-effect.
- Clean read on the 50–75 seat band that had been muddying the cut; the 75–200 v2 recut held as the cleaner comparator.
- No drift on the standard guardrails (sample ratio, support-ticket posture, email/template QA from the Monday noise).

Expected timing. Third post-ship cohort window ≈ week of April 24, 2023. No "fixed" call before that read. Anything beyond cohort 3 (redefinitional change to 75–200 v2, the institutional Feb–Apr writeup for the May 12 all-hands) was downstream of, not a substitute for, that third clean cohort.

Helio Start archive note — original sub-50-seat effort

Purpose: onboarding and retrospective reference for the original Helio Start motion that culminated in the March 18, 2024 bounded GA. This note records duration, core workstreams, and how commercial guardrails were meant to relate to eligibility and product constraints. It is descriptive history, not a current operating plan.

1. Duration

The original sub-50-seat effort ran from June 2023 pre-discovery through the March 18, 2024 bounded general-availability launch on the public pricing page — roughly nine months end to end.

- June 2023: pre-discovery readout ("Helio Start pre-discovery readout — measurement spine"). "Helio Start" established as a working name, not a launch promise or pricing-page commitment.
- June 22, 2023: leadership readout framed guarded pre-discovery through July.
- June 28, 2023: accepted decision captured — guarded pre-discovery through July; August beta conditional on eligibility, instrumentation, lifecycle, and support gates; old "Q3 Launch Path" framing retired.
- July 2023: instrumentation, refusal-rule, and lifecycle-fork work; refusal-rule copy drafted for migration, agency-shared-admin, manual billing, and heavy-support conditions.
- August 7, 2023: controlled-beta readiness workback. Beta opened in August as a narrow, manually reviewed cohort with no public pricing-page entry, no paid acquisition, and no Q3 revenue guarantee.
- August 11, 2023: first live beta admissions for under-50 teams with the established gates.
- December 2023: Helio Start still a small, manually reviewed invite cohort, separate from the ordinary-starter v3 dashboard.
- January 18, 2024: readiness decision approved a capped 120-application controlled-readiness cohort drawn from the waitlist and referral pool; every application reviewed; refusal rules preserved; test of operating capacity, not forecastable acquisition.
- February 26, 2024: results decision. 120 applications broke out as 76 auto-passed exact-match admin proofs, 28 legitimate mismatches passed with corroborating admin evidence, and 16 routed out for agency identity, unresolved ownership, manual billing, import, or migration needs. Of 104 admitted accounts, 82 created workspaces and 68 reached first integration by day seven. Supported a bounded public-product decision, not immediate GA and not removal of refusal boundaries.
- March 4, 2024: Tomás approved bounded March 18 GA on the public pricing page; paid acquisition and forecastable pipeline language stayed out. Priya expanded remit to the full self-serve operating model.
- March 5, 2024: operating-plan doc requested before Friday.
- March 18, 2024: bounded GA live on the public pricing page. Live smoke test admitted the simple under-50 workspace with verified admin access, supported billing, current entitlement state, and first-week integration fit; manual-billing case routed to assisted; agency case ineligible; unresolved-ownership case stayed pending.

The original effort closed at the March 18, 2024 bounded GA. Subsequent maturity cohorts, connector-access release, paid-test reviews, and capped paid-acquisition proposals are downstream of that GA, not part of the original effort.

2. Core workstreams

The work was organized around five workstreams, with explicit owner lanes set at the March 4, 2024 decision and carried into the March 5 operating plan.

- Eligibility and refusal rules. Worked the public admission conditions (admin proof, deployment simplicity, first-week integration fit, current entitlement state, supported billing) and the route-out conditions (agency identities, manual billing, imports, migrations, unsupported permissions, unresolved ownership). Corroborating-evidence path preserved for legitimate domain mismatches. Refusal framing was held as "protecting customers from a failed self-serve setup," not "bad fit."
- Entitlement and support-state instrumentation (Daniela). Clean event taxonomy and entitlement instrumentation for admin complexity, import or migration help, support handoff, and entitlement state. `billing_account_mode` set at workspace creation with no plan-name inference. Backfill policy `entitlement_source=ops_review_2023_08_01` documented for early-trial workspaces that lacked the field at creation. Stored connector-authentication answer separately from Helio admin proof. Held a current entitlement and support-state audit guard at every admission.
- Activation and support-load measurement (Owen). Activation definition v3, first integration within seven days divided by all eligible starts. Support load measured as ordinary setup questions plus permissions or ownership reviews per 100 eligible starts, with pre-activation contacts included. Routed-before-setup cases and entitlement or support-state failures kept as separate counts rather than disappearing inside a rate. Reporting kept separate from retained mid-segment v2 and Expansion Assist; the 50-75 seat band shown separately. Support load held as a first-class metric beside activation, not subordinated to it.
- Lifecycle copy and risk controls (Ines). Conservative lifecycle fork, audience checks held until manual review approved each account, no proxy automation for state-changing branches. Two education touches held in draft. Refusal copy drafted to frame exclusions as protecting customers from a failed self-serve setup.
- Customer Success routed-before-setup path and operating capacity. Docs-first help for ordinary failed integrations, assisted routing for support-heavy cases. Held capacity as the binding constraint on cohort sizing and on any future capped paid run; operating-capacity test, not forecastable acquisition.

Cross-functional lane (Riley): executive language, eligibility and product constraints, lifecycle and support boundaries, and cross-surface decisions. Operated as an operating model across existing roles, not a new team.

Sequence that bound the workstreams: eligibility/refusal before packaging; taxonomy/entitlements before pricing-page experiment; lifecycle fork before paid acquisition; activation measurement kept separate from retained mid-segment throughout.

3. Commercial guardrails relative to eligibility and product constraints

The design intent was that commercial guardrails never softened eligibility or product constraints; the constraints were the guardrails. Three relationships defined that intent.

- Pricing-page copy was constrained by eligibility, not the other way around. The original "Under 50 seats? Start instantly — no review required" subhead was rejected because it implied launch timing and a no-review admission when unsupported applicants actually routed to assistance or were found ineligible, and admitted accounts still had to satisfy admin-proof, connector, external-authority, entitlement, billing, and simple-deployment requirements. The approved March 7, 2024 pricing-page copy ("Helio Start for straightforward teams under 50," with body requiring admin access, supported billing, and a first-week-connectable first integration, CTA "Check eligibility") was treated as accurate only because the underlying eligibility and refusal rules were already in place.
- Eligibility and refusal rules were the product constraints that bounded commercial exposure. Agency identities, manual billing, imports, migrations, and unsupported permissions were route-out conditions, not conversion targets. Refusal framing was held as protecting customers from a failed self-serve setup. The readiness-cohort routing (76 auto-passed, 28 corroborated, 16 routed out) was treated as evidence the constraints were operating, not as friction to be optimized away.
- Paid acquisition and forecastable pipeline language stayed separate from product-readiness. Paid acquisition, public signup, pricing-page exposure, pipeline credit, and launch language were each a distinct gate, none of them authorized by product readiness alone. Marcus's acceptance that the readiness cohort was a test of operating capacity rather than forecastable acquisition was an explicit condition, not a courtesy. Cohort sizing was bounded by Customer Success capacity, not by demand.

Three product constraints were held as non-negotiable through the original effort and into the bounded GA:

- Current entitlement state as an admission gate (Daniela's instrumentation and audit guard).
- Supported billing only; manual billing routed to assisted.
- Connector authentication stored separately from Helio admin proof, with external-authority meaning preserved.

These three constraints carried directly into the March 18, 2024 live smoke test: the simple under-50 case was admitted because it satisfied all three plus admin access and first-week integration fit; the manual-billing case routed out; the agency case was ineligible; the unresolved-ownership case stayed pending rather than entering a workspace.

4. What this note is not

This note does not establish current operating evidence, current cohort numbers, or current paid-acquisition state. It does not substitute for the May 24, 2024 review pre-read, the January 2025 Q1 operating-review read, the January 13, 2027 paid-test decision frame, the 2027 paid-acquisition working drafts, or the Q1 2026 quarterly board operating evidence intake. Anything dated after March 18, 2024 belongs to the post-GA operating period, not to the original effort.

5. Pointers to source artifacts

- Helio Start pre-discovery readout — measurement spine (doc_1789215501545).
- Helio Start leadership readout — Jun 22 (June 20, 2023 readout).
- Helio Start readiness cohort — February 26 preread.
- Helio Start public-product decision (March 4, 2024).
- Helio Start bounded GA — March 18 operating plan.
- Helio Start readiness cohort — results decision (February 26, 2024).
- May 24, 2024 continuation-gate brief.

Refusal framing was held as protecting customers from a failed self-serve setup. The readiness-cohort routing (76 auto-passed, 28 corroborated, 16 routed out) was treated as evidence the constraints were operating, not as friction to be optimized away.
- Paid acquisition and forecastable pipeline language stayed separate from product-readiness. Paid acquisition, public signup, pricing-page exposure, pipeline credit, and launch language were each a distinct gate, none of them authorized by product readiness alone. Marcus's acceptance that the readiness cohort was a test of operating capacity rather than forecastable acquisition was an explicit condition, not a courtesy. Cohort sizing was bounded by Customer Success capacity, not by demand.

Three product constraints were held as non-negotiable through the original effort and into the bounded GA:

- Current entitlement state as an admission gate (Daniela's instrumentation and audit guard).
- Supported billing only; manual billing routed to assisted.
- Connector authentication stored separately from Helio admin proof, with external-authority meaning preserved.

These three constraints carried directly into the March 18, 2024 live smoke test: the simple under-50 case was admitted because it satisfied all three plus admin access and first-week integration fit; the manual-billing case routed out; the agency case was ineligible; the unresolved-ownership case stayed pending rather than entering a workspace.

4. What this note is not

This note does not establish current operating evidence, current cohort numbers, or current paid-acquisition state. It does not substitute for the May 24, 2024 review pre-read, the January 2025 Q1 operating-review read, the January 13, 2027 paid-test decision frame, the 2027 paid-acquisition working drafts, or the Q1 2026 quarterly board operating evidence intake. Anything dated after March 18, 2024 belongs to the post-GA operating period, not to the original effort.

input.body:
PRE-DESIGN INTAKE CHECKLIST — Growth or Customer Success lifecycle decisioning
Reusable. Run before any design, copy, routing, or experiment work that touches a lifecycle event, wording change, eligibility rule, or audience/scope expansion. Owner: requesting human admin (Growth or CS). Reviewer: second qualifying human admin.

0. PREREQUISITE — signed-off scope card
   Required to proceed: a written, dated scope card signed by the requesting admin AND a second qualifying human admin, containing all five fields below. Without the full card signed off, design MAY NOT proceed. There is no advisory mode. If anything below is missing, stale, unresolved, or in conflict with an active CS thread, the work stops at intake and goes back to the requester.

   0.1 Consumer — exact, bounded population. One named cohort, no "any logged-in member," no "all eligible users." State inclusion and exclusion. No 6th consumer unless explicitly approved.
   0.2 Lifecycle event — the exact event being decided (release, eligibility change, enrollment, reminder, handoff, escalation, lapse, renewal, etc.). No adjacent events implied.
   0.3 Surface — exact wording, copy, routing, eligibility rule, experiment variant, or rollback path being changed. Anything not named is unchanged.
   0.4 Entitlement — current entitlement pulled from the authoritative source at intake (not from memory, not from a prior card). Note source, date, and the human who confirmed.
   0.5 Conflict check — confirmation that no active CS thread, open complaint, ongoing escalation, or in-flight experiment covers the same surface. If one exists, the work pauses and is reconciled with CS first.

1. SUPPORTS (only fill after 0 is signed off)
   1.1 Success measure — how we know it worked, and the bound (who counts, over what window).
   1.2 Rollback — explicit path back to current wording/routing/eligibility, with owner and time window.
   1.3 Owner-auth map — which human admin can approve which sub-change. No batched auto-approval of entitlements. No silent consumer additions.
   1.4 Communication plan — which surfaces notify the consumer, in what cadence, and who sends.
   1.5 Post-design QA — heavier loop on risky paths (where a broken branch hits many users fast); lighter on copy/order only.

2. GATE DECISION (plain)
   Design MAY proceed before the prerequisite is satisfied: NO.
   Design MAY proceed only after all five fields in section 0 are present, current, and signed by two qualifying human admins, with no active CS conflict on the same surface. If any field is missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting, intake returns the request to the owner; design does not start.

3. OUT OF SCOPE (reminder so this card stays bounded)
   - Adding a consumer that wasn't named in 0.1.
   - Changing wording, CS handling, event, eligibility, routing, or rollback that wasn't named in 0.3.
   - Running an experiment that wasn't named in 0.3.
   - Bundling an entitlement change with the lifecycle change.
   - Treating a "sounds like" match in another consumer's record as approval to act.

(Maintained by Riley. Team may route updates per the buckets below; everything else comes to Riley.)

Three content categories:
  1. Readout-shape
  2. Examples (the numbers inside a readout)
  3. Lifecycle-risk

1. Readout-shape
   What it covers: the structure of periodic reports — closed-batch panels, cohort readouts, the standing self-review and monitoring docs. Which lines appear, in what order, with what labels.

   Team may route:
     - Reordering, renaming, or relabeling existing lines
     - Adding a new line derived from a field already collected in the existing source
     - Removing a line that has been documented as obsolete for ≥1 closed cycle
     - Correcting a transcription error in a label or heading

   Escalate to Riley:
     - Adding a line whose source is not already collected
     - Changing the meaning or scope of an existing line
     - Any change that affects what gets reported to a stakeholder (Growth, Finance, etc.)

2. Examples
   What it covers: the concrete numbers inside a readout — admitted counts, contact incidences, activation numerators/denominators, batch spend, monitor outcomes.

   Team may route:
     - Filling in numbers from an already-closed batch or cycle
     - Interim numerator/denominator cleanups (e.g. reclassifying a small panel) that do not change the closed-batch totals
     - Carrying forward prior-cycle figures into the current cycle's template

   Escalate to Riley:
     - Any change that alters a closed-batch total or certified spend
     - Forecast, pipeline, mature-outcome, or paid-batch credit decisions
     - Decisions about whether a number supports a customer-outcome claim
     - Invoice classification (whether an invoice receives pipeline / forecast / outcome treatment)

3. Lifecycle-risk
   What it covers: audience, eligibility, suppression, release authority, rollback, and any proposal that would expand a consumer's audience, change gating logic, or bypass an existing hold.

   Team may NOT route. Everything in this category comes to Riley, including:
     - Audience expansion (e.g. widening from qualifying human admin to any logged-in member)
     - Eligibility, preflight, or suppression-semantics changes
     - Release authority, rollback path, or experiment wiring
     - Sixth-consumer proposals or new email programs
     - Re-evaluation of a held or state-changing escalation
     - Any proposal Ines (or another owner) previously escalated as state-changing and not yet approved

General rules
   - When in doubt, escalate. A stakeholder request is not authorization.
   - Routable updates still need an owner log entry (date, author, what changed, why).
   - No update may be implemented, queued, staged, or scheduled until its bucket is confirmed.

tests.request: Create a historical growth brief for the mid-segment churn investigation’s pre-ruling H2 phase, using monthly churn as the metric of record. Include the active hypothesis, the planned historical comparison work, and the agreed owner and contents for each hypothesis-ruling one-pager, and label it clearly as a pre-ruling artifact.

input.body:
STATUS: PRE-RULING HISTORICAL ARTIFACT — recorded as the H2 phase before any hypothesis ruling is issued. Superseded by the ruling one-pager once H2 is decided; not a ruling.

1. ACTIVE HYPOTHESIS (H2)
   H2 — competitor cycle. The mid-segment churn lift observed in late Jan / Feb 2023 is attributable to a competitor-side promotional or contract-renewal cycle drawing mid-segment accounts away, independent of our pricing, onboarding timing, or CS coverage. H2 is one of four hypotheses in the Feb–Apr 2023 mid-segment churn investigation (alongside H1 pricing artifact, H3 onboarding timing, H4 CS coverage gap) and is being run in parallel; no hypothesis has been ruled in or out at this stage.

2. METRIC OF RECORD
   Monthly churn, mid-segment cohort. Monthly grain is the metric of record for the investigation as a whole and is what the H2 ruling one-pager will rule against. No weekly or rolling-window substitution for H2; any smoothed view is supporting only.

3. PLANNED HISTORICAL COMPARISON WORK (H2, pre-ruling)
   The H2 phase before ruling is built around historical comparison work, not a forward causal claim. The planned comparisons, all on monthly churn at the mid-segment cut:
   a. Same-segment monthly churn in the prior two comparable windows (a year-prior comparable window and the most recent non-anomalous comparable window). Purpose: establish whether a competitor-cycle lift of this magnitude has a historical analog.
   b. Same-segment monthly churn during the last documented prior competitor promotional / renewal cycle we can identify from historical notes. Purpose: shape-match against a known cycle, not just a magnitude match.
   c. Same-segment monthly churn in matched prior windows where a competitor cycle was NOT present. Purpose: counterfactual baseline so H2's lift is not over-attributed to cycle noise.
   d. Cross-segment sanity: monthly churn in adjacent segments during the same historical windows, to confirm any H2-attributed lift is mid-segment-specific and not a market-wide move misread as a competitor effect.
   e. Source / lineage check on the historical windows used in (a)–(d) — same data source and same cohort definition as the current investigation, so the comparison is apples-to-apples and not a methodology-mix artifact.
   Historical-comparison work runs before any H2 ruling; results feed the ruling one-pager rather than pre-deciding it.

4. H2-RULING ONE-PAGER — AGREED OWNERS AND CONTENTS
   Single one-pager, produced once H2 is ruled, signed off before issue. Pre-ruling phase records the agreed shape; the artifact itself is not written here.

   Owner: Riley (overall H2 ruling accountability, same role as on the other hypotheses in this investigation).

   Contents agreed for the ruling one-pager:
   a. Ruling statement — H2 ruled in, ruled out, or ruled partial, in plain language, dated.
   b. Metric of record restated — monthly churn, mid-segment, same cohort cut as the pre-ruling work.
   c. Historical comparison results — the (a)–(e) comparisons above, each with the window, the monthly-churn figure, and the read. This is the body of evidence the ruling rests on.
   d. Magnitude and shape read — whether the current lift matches a historical competitor cycle on size, shape, and segment-specificity, or whether the historical comparisons argue against H2.
   e. Counterfactual note — explicit statement of what the matched non-cycle historical windows looked like, so the ruling does not over-attribute.
   f. Boundary statement — what H2 does and does not explain relative to H1 / H3 / H4 (e.g. even if H2 rules in, the residual attributable to pricing, onboarding, or CS coverage is left for those one-pagers).
   g. Limitations and data-lineage caveats carried over from (e) above.
   h. Sign-off line — Riley, dated, with a one-line note that this is the H2 ruling and supersedes the pre-ruling historical brief.

   No ruling one-pager is being authored in this pre-ruling artifact; this section records the agreed shape only.

5. WHAT THIS ARTIFACT IS AND IS NOT
   Is: the historical record of the H2 pre-ruling phase — the active hypothesis, the planned historical comparison work, and the agreed owner and contents of the ruling one-pager.
   Is not: the H2 ruling, a forecast, a forward causal claim, or a substitute for the ruling one-pager. Once H2 is ruled, the ruling one-pager supersedes this artifact.

6. CROSS-HYPOTHESIS NOTE
   The other three hypotheses in this investigation (H1 pricing artifact, H3 onboarding timing, H4 CS coverage gap) follow the same shape — active hypothesis, planned comparison work, agreed ruling one-pager — and each will get its own pre-ruling historical record and its own ruling one-pager. H2 is recorded here independently and is not pre-decided by work on the others.

Scope: applies ONLY to the pricing page under active experiment (flagged via `pricing_page_*` exposure key). Other pages, surfaces, and downstream flows are not constrained by this checklist.

While a pricing-page experiment is running, no other layout / UI / structural changes are allowed on the tested page. Rationale: concurrent on-page changes muddy attribution (see EXP-2023-02-pricing-page / `pricing_page_2023q2_rev`, confounded by the Mar 2 signup-form change).

BLOCKED on the tested pricing page
- Layout, spacing, visual hierarchy, or component positioning changes
- New, removed, or reordered UI components (cards, tables, toggles, sections)
- Styling changes that visibly shift visual weight or prominence (color, size, emphasis)
- Any change that would force a redesign vs. analysis of the original variant

ALLOWED on the tested pricing page
- Copy / wording changes (headlines, labels, microcopy, tooltips)
- Pricing, plan, or packaging-content changes (the variable under test)
- Experiment-config changes: traffic split, exposure rule, targeting, rollout %
- Instrumentation: events, properties, PostHog exposures, segment definitions
- Bug fixes that restore intended behavior (must be logged + reviewed before ship)
- Accessibility fixes that don't shift visual prominence
- Content additions / removals (e.g., FAQ entries) that don't reposition existing elements
- Tracking or analytics-only changes with no user-visible effect

OUT OF SCOPE (do not apply this rule)
- Other pages on the site
- Onboarding, signup, checkout, or post-purchase flows
- Email, push, or other off-page surfaces
- Admin / internal tools

Process
- Before shipping any change to the tested page, check: does it touch layout / UI / structure? If yes, defer to after the experiment window closes or queue for the next post-period cleanup.
- If a blocked change is deemed necessary mid-experiment, pause the experiment, ship the change, restart cleanly — do not co-run.
- Log any allowed-but-noteworthy change in the experiment doc (hypothesis → confounders section).
- At experiment close, the rule lifts; post-period layout cleanups resume per normal release process.

Last updated: 2028-01-01

input.body:
# Audit Worksheet — Q4 2023 Expansion Assist Shadow Decisions on Retained Mid-Segment Accounts

Period under review: 2023-10-01 through 2023-12-31
Scope: Shadow decisions issued by Expansion Assist against retained mid-segment accounts, evaluated against the Customer Success suppression check and the evidence combination required before a commercial prompt could be considered at the time.
Prepared: 2028-01-01
Prepared by: Riley (via Hermes)
Status: Draft — pending source-ledger attachment and ruleset confirmation

---

## 1. Ruleset Confirmation (Q4 2023, as in force)

Before populating the per-account table, confirm the exact rule text from the Q4 2023 archive. The reconstruction below is based on prior precedent; flag any divergence from the archive.

### 1.1 Customer Success Suppression Check
A commercial prompt for Expansion Assist must be SUPPRESSED when ANY of the following holds at the moment of decision:
- An active Customer Success (CS) case is open against the account, OR
- The account is currently in an unresolved CS escalation state, OR
- A conflicting CS signal exists (e.g. open complaint + expansion offer issued in the same window).

Suppression verdict on any of the above → no commercial prompt permitted regardless of evidence combo.

### 1.2 Evidence Combination Required Before a Commercial Prompt Could Be Considered
At minimum, ALL of the following must be present and current (not stale):
- (E1) Retained-account status confirmation for the mid-segment cohort
- (E2) Qualifying-human-admin entitlement record, current as of decision date
- (E3) Bounded operation credential (op) record for the shadow decision
- (E4) Bounded claim evidence (claim) record referencing the same account + admin
- (E5) Shadow-decision log entry with timestamp, decisioning admin, and routing context
- (E6) Adherence to the 5-consumer concurrent-prompt limit at decision time

Missing / stale / unresolved / conflicting on any of E1–E6 → HOLD (do not issue commercial prompt).

### 1.3 Rule-Version Discrepancy Log
| Field | Reconstructed (precedent) | Archive value | Match? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Suppression trigger set | open CS / unresolved / conflicting | [pending] | [ ] |
| Evidence items required | E1–E6 above | [pending] | [ ] |
| Stale threshold | [pending] | [pending] | [ ] |
| 5-consumer limit in force Q4 2023 | assumed yes | [pending] | [ ] |
| Shadow → commercial handoff gate | shadow-decision log present | [pending] | [ ] |

If any cell does not match, restate the audit criteria in §2 against the archive value before scoring.

---

## 2. Audit Criteria (Verdict Logic)

For each shadow decision reviewed:

- VOID — Suppression condition (§1.1) was true and a commercial prompt was nevertheless issued or staged.
- HOLD — No suppression condition, but one or more evidence items in §1.2 were missing / stale / unresolved / conflicting. Correct outcome: no commercial prompt. Verify none was issued.
- CLEAN — No suppression condition AND all evidence items present and current AND within 5-consumer limit AND shadow log present. Commercial prompt permitted under the rule.
- INSUFFICIENT DATA — Source ledger does not permit verdict (mark and escalate).

---

## 3. Per-Account Review

Source ledger: [path / query — to be attached]
Cohort filter: mid-segment, retained status during Q4 2023

| # | Account ID | Segment | Retained Q4? | Shadow decisions in window | Suppression state at each decision | Evidence combo (E1–E6) | 5-consumer limit OK? | Verdict | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [id] | mid | Y/N | [count, dates] | [open CS / unresolved / conflicting / none — per decision] | [present/missing per item, per decision] | Y/N | VOID/HOLD/CLEAN/INSUFFICIENT | |
| 2 | [id] | mid | Y/N | | | | | | |
| 3 | [id] | mid | Y/N | | | | | | |
| … | | | | | | | | | |

Row-count target: equal to distinct retained mid-segment accounts receiving ≥1 shadow decision in Q4 2023. If the source ledger is unavailable, leave row 1 as the template and note "source not attached — table to be populated from archive".

---

## 4. Per-Decision Detail (for VOID and HOLD findings only)

For each non-CLEAN verdict, capture enough detail to support a remediation memo:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Account ID | |
| Shadow decision timestamp | |
| Decisioning admin | |
| Suppression trigger (if VOID) | |
| Missing / stale evidence items (if HOLD) | |
| Was a commercial prompt issued despite verdict? | Y/N |
| Prompt issuance timestamp (if Y) | |
| Customer-impact summary | |
| Linked CS case ID (if any) | |
| Routing context | |

---

## 5. Aggregate Findings (to be computed once §3 is populated)

- Total shadow decisions reviewed: [n]
- Distinct accounts reviewed: [n]
- CLEAN: [n] ([%])
- HOLD: [n] ([%])
- VOID: [n] ([%])
- INSUFFICIENT DATA: [n] ([%])
- Commercial prompts issued under VOID: [n] — severity: HIGH
- Commercial prompts issued under HOLD: [n] — severity: HIGH
- Suppression-rule bypasses: [n]
- Evidence-combo shortfalls (most common missing item): [E#]
- 5-consumer-limit exceedances: [n]
- Cross-decision patterns (admin, account, time-of-day, cohort): [pending analysis]

A non-zero count in either VOID or commercial-prompt-issued-under-HOLD rows escalates this audit from informational to remediation-required.

---

## 6. Remediation Actions

input.body:
Source: archived investigation doc "Mid-segment churn investigation Feb–Apr 2023 — what we learned" (institutional writeup started Apr 29, 2023; circulated for the May 12 all-hands). This crosswalk preserves the original H1–H4 ordering as it was enumerated in the investigation Notion doc on Feb 8, 2023, so that later numbered references in A/B design docs, the rule-out log, the institutional writeup, and post-stabilization retros can be decoded against the same anchor terms.

Cohort of record for the investigation: mid-segment v1 (50–200 paid seats) for the hypothesis-ruling period Feb 7–Apr 26, 2023. Mid-segment v2 (75–200 paid seats) is the cohort of record from the Apr 26 settlement onward. Both cuts are retained in the warehouse; comparators against the Feb–Apr window are explicitly on v1, not v2.

Original hypothesis stack (Feb 8, 2023 ordering):
  H1 — Pricing artifact (tier-segmented pricing / contract-mix effect on mid-segment churn).
  H2 — Competitor cycle / seasonal (external market action or generic Feb seasonality).
  H3 — Onboarding timing (late-Dec / early-Jan starts maturing into churn on a lag; day-7 touch landing at the wrong relative point in the flow).
  H4 — CS coverage gap (CSM load drift leaving a coverage hole in mid-segment).
  Fifth (unnumbered) — Early-Jan ship / product regression (kept on the board as a residual possibility; never formally assigned an H5 label in the doc or rule-out log).

Decision anchors:
  H1 — Ruled dead Feb 14, 2023. Tier-segmented pass on mid-segment v1: entry 5.0%, standard 5.2%, plus 5.1% (≈20 bps spread). If pricing/contract mix were driving the spike, entry would have been the outlier and the other two would have sat closer to baseline. Did not happen. Owen 1-pager drafted Feb 15. H1 downgrades from "primary suspect" to "background possibility, cannot fully rule out but unlikely to be the main story."
  H2 — Ruled dead Feb 20, 2023. Same-window comps with the same cohort logic as the Jan scan plus Owen's morning check: Feb 2022 mid-segment monthly churn 2.2%, Feb 2021 2.0%. No historical version of the spike at that window. Competitor-cycle and generic-seasonal explanations fail. Posted to #growth-investigations Feb 21.
  H3 — Confirmed real Feb 28, 2023. Activation-day cut instead of plain calendar day, same cohort logic as the Jan scan plus Owen check, n=210. Pre-onboarding-activation cohort 3.1% churn; post-day-7-pre-activation cohort 7.8%. 4.7-point gap is too wide to hand-wave as noise. Mechanism: day-7 lifecycle touch firing on calendar day rather than activation state, punting users who are still drifting. Operationalized Mar 1 as EXP-2023-02-onboarding-trigger (variant flag lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2, mid-segment only, target n=400, two-week powered run). Launched Mar 13 (eng review pushed it one day). Apr 10 post-ship weekly cut shows the v2 lift; Apr 17 second-post-ship cohort dips to +1.4 pts — root cause is a separate CS auto-onboarding-nudge outage Apr 12–15 on Daniela's side (phase shift, contained), not the onboarding-trigger A/B.
  H4 — Kept on the board through Feb 21 and not ruled dead in the rule-out log under the original numbering. No later internal source retires or renumbers H4 against the original Feb 8 anchor. Coverage-math framing (CSM load drift leaving a coverage hole) is preserved verbatim in the institutional writeup.
  Fifth (unnumbered) — Early-Jan ship / product regression. Kept on the board as a residual possibility, never promoted to a formal H5 number and never formally retired in the rule-out log.

Crosswalk notes for readers decoding later numbered references:
  1. H1–H4 map 1:1 to the anchors above. There is no later renumbering on file. If a later doc refers to "Hypothesis 1" in connection with the Feb–Apr 2023 investigation, it is the pricing-artifact hypothesis unless the doc explicitly states otherwise.
  2. The early-Jan regression fifth was deliberately left unnumbered to keep Marcus's parallel pricing-page track (EXP pricing_page_2023q2_rev) from smearing over the formal hypothesis stack. Treat any later "H5" reference to the Feb–Apr 2023 investigation as informal at best and verify against the original doc before quoting.

This crosswalk preserves the original H1–H4 ordering as it was enumerated in the investigation Notion doc on Feb 8, 2023, so that later numbered references in A/B design docs, the rule-out log, the institutional writeup, and post-stabilization retros can be decoded against the same anchor terms.

Cohort of record for the investigation: mid-segment v1 (50–200 paid seats) for the hypothesis-ruling period Feb 7–Apr 26, 2023. Mid-segment v2 (75–200 paid seats) is the cohort of record from the Apr 26 settlement onward. Both cuts are retained in the warehouse; comparators against the Feb–Apr window are explicitly on v1, not v2.

Original hypothesis stack (Feb 8, 2023 ordering):
  H1 — Pricing artifact (tier-segmented pricing / contract-mix effect on mid-segment churn).
  H2 — Competitor cycle / seasonal (external market action or generic Feb seasonality).
  H3 — Onboarding timing (late-Dec / early-Jan starts maturing into churn on a lag; day-7 touch landing at the wrong relative point in the flow).
  H4 — CS coverage gap (CSM load drift leaving a coverage hole in mid-segment).
  Fifth (unnumbered) — Early-Jan ship / product regression (kept on the board as a residual possibility; never formally assigned an H5 label in the doc or rule-out log).

Decision anchors:
  H1 — Ruled dead Feb 14, 2023. Tier-segmented pass on mid-segment v1: entry 5.0%, standard 5.2%, plus 5.1% (≈20 bps spread). If pricing/contract mix were driving the spike, entry would have been the outlier and the other two would have sat closer to baseline. Did not happen. Owen 1-pager drafted Feb 15. H1 downgrades from "primary suspect" to "background possibility, cannot fully rule out but unlikely to be the main story."
  H2 — Ruled dead Feb 20, 2023. Same-window comps with the same cohort logic as the Jan scan plus Owen's morning check: Feb 2022 mid-segment monthly churn 2.2%, Feb 2021 2.0%. No historical version of the spike at that window. Competitor-cycle and generic-seasonal explanations fail. Posted to #growth-investigations Feb 21.
  H3 — Confirmed real Feb 28, 2023. Activation-day cut instead of plain calendar day, same cohort logic as the Jan scan plus Owen check, n=210. Pre-onboarding-activation cohort 3.1% churn; post-day-7-pre-activation cohort 7.8%. 4.7-point gap is too wide to hand-wave as noise. Mechanism: day-7 lifecycle touch firing on calendar day rather than activation state, punting users who are still drifting. Operationalized Mar 1 as EXP-2023-02-onboarding-trigger (variant flag lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2, mid-segment only, target n=400, two-week powered run). Launched Mar 13 (eng review pushed it one day). Apr 10 post-ship weekly cut shows the v2 lift; Apr 17 second-post-ship cohort dips to +1.4 pts — root cause is a separate CS auto-onboarding-nudge outage Apr 12–15 on Daniela's side (phase shift, contained), not the onboarding-trigger A/B.
  H4 — Kept on the board through Feb 21 and not ruled dead in the rule-out log under the original numbering. No later internal source retires or renumbers H4 against the original Feb 8 anchor. Coverage-math framing (CSM load drift leaving a coverage hole) is preserved verbatim in the institutional writeup.

  6. Helio Start and Expansion Assist are explicitly out of scope for this investigation and its hypothesis stack. The May 12 all-hands material and the institutional writeup keep retained-mid, Helio Start, and Expansion Assist on separate rails.

input.body:
Document type: Historical design-hypothesis card.
Status: ORIGINAL DESIGN HYPOTHESIS — pre-launch intent, NOT an observed result.
Experiment ID: EXP-2023-02-pricing-page
Hypothesis recorded: 2023-02-26.
Planned launch window: from 2023-03-07 (subject to Daniela engineering review).
PostHog feature flag placeholder: `pricing_page_2023q2_rev` (registered, not rolled out at hypothesis time).

------------------------------------------------------------
1. Treatment concept (what the variant changed)
------------------------------------------------------------
A simplified pricing-page layout paired with an explicit value-per-seat framing.
- Simplified layout: reduced visual complexity on the pricing page versus the then-current control.
- Explicit value-per-seat framing: each plan presented with a stated value-per-seat articulation rather than only headline price.
- Registered as PostHog feature flag `pricing_page_2023q2_rev`; flag was a placeholder at hypothesis time and was not yet rolled out.

------------------------------------------------------------
2. Target customer tiers (who the treatment was intended to move)
------------------------------------------------------------
- Starter tier.
- Growth tier.
These two tiers were the named conversion targets in the original hypothesis. No other tier was named.

------------------------------------------------------------
3. Intended conversion outcome (what success was defined to look like)
------------------------------------------------------------
- Increase Starter and Growth tier conversion.
- The intended outcome was framed as a directional lift in conversion for those two tiers, not as a change in activation, support load, ticket volume, or any other secondary metric.

------------------------------------------------------------
4. Minimum lift (the threshold the hypothesis was committed to)
------------------------------------------------------------
- At least +1.5 percentage points in Starter and Growth conversion versus control.
- This is the minimum-effect threshold the original hypothesis committed to. It is the bar the variant had to clear, not a forecast and not an observed result.

------------------------------------------------------------
5. Important labeling — read this before quoting any number from this card
------------------------------------------------------------
- Everything on this card is the ORIGINAL DESIGN HYPOTHESIS as recorded on 2023-02-26, before launch.
- No observed lift, no observed null, no p-value, no confidence interval, and no cohort read appears on this card by design.
- The first-week peek, the December first cohort read, the stabilization cohort read, the combined read, and any subsequent discussion of the result belong on a separate result card. Do not import those numbers into this card.
- The original hypothesis and the later result are intentionally split across two cards so the hypothesis can be cited on its own terms.

------------------------------------------------------------
6. Known confound noted at hypothesis time (recorded for context only)
------------------------------------------------------------
- A concurrent 2023-03-02 signup-form layout change was flagged as a risk to isolating the pricing-page variable. This is a methodological caveat about the design, not a revision of the hypothesis itself, and does not change the treatment concept, target tiers, intended outcome, or minimum lift stated above.

------------------------------------------------------------
7. Roles at hypothesis time
------------------------------------------------------------
- Design / hypothesis owner: Riley.
- Engineering review and release control: Daniela.
- Forecast ownership: Marcus Vail.
- PostHog flag registration: `pricing_page_2023q2_rev` (placeholder, not rolled).

tests.answer:
Strong context. The key constraints carry forward cleanly:

- Entitlement instrumentation is a hard gate before pricing-page test or launch.
- No concurrent layout/UI change alongside a pricing-page test.
- Activation def v3 stays for under-50; 75–200-seat mid-seg v2 stays separate; show 50–75 band separately.
- Support load is first-class next to activation.
- Paid acquisition and forecastable pipeline language were deliberately held back at GA approval — they don't fall out automatically.
- Sales/pipeline, refusal routes, lifecycle state-changes, and support handoff have all been sequenced the same way each prior cycle.

Now the checklist.

HELIO START — CHANGE-SEQUENCING CHECKLIST (2028)
For: packaging, pricing-page experiment, paid acquisition, activation measurement.

Rule of sequencing: each block below must be settled (not "in flight," not "drafted") before the next block can do work that depends on it. Where the order is the load-bearing part, I say so explicitly.

  1. ENTITLEMENT INSTRUMENTATION (must be settled first, full stop)
     Why it goes first: every later block — packaging copy, pricing-page routing, paid-acquisition targeting, activation numerators/denominators, support-handoff triggers — reads from entitlement state. If the state is wrong or inferred, the experiment measures the wrong population and paid acquisition buys the wrong accounts.
     What "settled" means:
       - billing_account_mode captured at workspace creation
       - support_handoff_created / support_handoff_confirmed / manual_billing_exception_added firing on the right paths
       - no plan-name inference anywhere in the activation or support-load pipelines
       - one-time backfill labeled (entitlement_source = ops_review_<date>) so historical rows aren't mistaken for native signal
       - refusal routes (migration / import / unsupported permissions / manual billing) documented as refusal events, not silent drops
     Blocks until done: packaging (can't write truthful eligibility copy), pricing-page experiment (can't define who sees Check eligibility vs. assisted routing), paid acquisition (can't target or exclude correctly), activation measurement (numerator/denominator is contaminated), support-load measurement (refusals won't appear as refusals).

  2. ELIGIBILITY & REFUSAL ROUTING (must be settled before packaging copy is final, before any pricing-page exposure)
     Why second: packaging copy on the pricing page and the experiment's audience both depend on a stable, written definition of who self-serves and who routes out. Without this, "Helio Start" is a label doing eligibility work it shouldn't.
     What "settled" means:
       - sub-50-seat rule written down, with the 50–75 band carved out as its own band (not folded into sub-50)
       - admin proof, deployment simplicity, first-week integration fit, current entitlement state, supported billing conditions each have a yes/no check
       - refusal routes (agency identities, manual billing, imports, migrations, unsupported permissions) confirmed as routes-out, not routes-into-self-serve
       - corroborating-evidence path for legitimate domain mismatches documented
     Blocks until done: pricing-page experiment (audience definition), paid acquisition (targeting and exclusions), packaging (the headline can only say "straightforward teams under 50" once "straightforward" is defined).

  3. PACKAGING (settled before the pricing-page experiment goes live)
     Why third: the pricing page is the surface; packaging is the substance under it. If packaging moves during the experiment, you can't tell whether a lift came from the experiment or from the offer.
     What "settled" means:
       - working name confirmed or replaced; customer-facing label doesn't imply launch timing or a cheaper plan
       - eligibility language matches the rule in block 2, not aspirational copy
       - refusal-path language points users to the correct assisted route
       - no pricing-page copy change is in flight concurrently with the experiment (per the standing no-concurrent-layout/UI-change rule)
     Blocks until done: pricing-page experiment (copy must be locked before the test starts), paid acquisition (creative claims must match settled packaging, not a draft).

  4. PRICING-PAGE EXPERIMENT (settled — i.e., read out — before paid acquisition opens)
     Why fourth and why before paid: the pricing page is the lowest-cost, lowest-volume surface. Paid acquisition multiplies whatever the page says, including its mistakes. Running paid against an unproven page buys the wrong accounts at speed.
     What "settled" means:
       - event taxonomy clean for the test (no concurrent UI/layout change)
       - audience = sub-50 with eligibility conditions met, refusal routes excluded
       - CTA ("Check eligibility" or equivalent) routes to the same eligibility check the instrumentation captures
       - readout: activation and support-load movement both reported; refusal rate reported; no overclaim in summary
     Blocks until done: paid acquisition (no traffic buying against an unread experiment), packaging finalization (the experiment may force a copy correction, which has to land before paid scales it).

  5. MEASUREMENT-POPULATION SEPARATION (must hold across all of the above; not a phase)
     This is not a step in the sequence — it is a rule the sequence has to preserve. Violating it invalidates everything downstream.
       - Sub-50 (Helio Start) measured on activation definition v3 only.
       - 75–200-seat mid-segment kept on v2; do not pool.
       - 50–75-seat band shown as its own band, never folded into sub-50.
       - Support load reported as a first-class metric beside activation; refusal events counted as refusals, not as activations or drops.
       - Retained mid-segment and Expansion Assist populations stay separate from Helio Start in every readout.
     Why it's called out separately: each prior sequencing slippage has been a population-pooling slippage. The experiment, paid acquisition, and the activation readout each have a default that wants to merge these for "cleaner numbers." Don't let them.

  6. PAID ACQUISITION (last; only opens after 1–5 are settled AND the pricing-page experiment has been read out)
     Why last: paid acquisition is a force multiplier on the pricing page. Until the page has been tested and the packaging behind it is final, paid traffic is buying against an untested offer and an unstable surface. The original GA approval deliberately held paid and forecastable pipeline language out of scope for exactly this reason.
     What "settled" / "ready" means:
       - pricing-page experiment read out with activation + support-load + refusal movement
       - packaging copy final, matching the experiment's outcome
       - targeting rules derived from settled entitlement/eligibility, with refusal routes as exclusions
       - no forecastable pipeline language reintroduced until paid has mature enough signal to support it
     Blocks until done: pipeline / forecast language (revisit only with mature paid-acquisition evidence); Expansion Assist or mid-segment motions being mistaken for Helio Start pipeline.

SEQUENCING SUMMARY
1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → (read out) → 6
└──────────── 5 (separation) runs across all of it

Sources: prior Helio Start decision / readout notes, the instrumentation-as-hard-gate decision, the no-concurrent-UI-change rule, activation v3 / mid-seg v2 / 50–75 band separation, refusal-route handling, and the original GA approval that kept paid acquisition and pipeline language out of scope.

messages.content: [2027-09-18T07:20:00-05:00] I arrived for one of my two permitted weekly runs and found the lake trail posted closed until noon for a scheduled event. I’m symptom-free, I haven’t run on a commute day, and I don’t want to add duration or frequency. What’s the more conservative same-day choice: wait until the trail reopens or use a flat ordinary-walking route? Keep the session at 35 easy minutes with the following-day symptom check, preserve the two-run nonconsecutive limit, and don’t add a bike day or advance the rehabilitation plan.

The more conservative same-day choice is the flat ordinary-walking route.

Why it's more conservative:
- Walking at 35 min easy is strictly below the running dose — lower impact, less ankle stress, lower musculoskeletal load than the established 35-min easy lake-trail run.
- A flat ordinary surface removes the trail-specific variables (unevenness, surface variation) that the lake trail carries, even though the lake trail has been tolerated cleanly.
- Dose goes down; route risk goes down. Both move in the conservative direction.

What this preserves (all of your constraints):
- 35 easy minutes — held.
- Same-day session with the following-morning symptom check — held.
- Two-run nonconsecutive weekly limit — held (a walk doesn't consume a run slot; both run slots remain available for the week on nonconsecutive days).
- No bike day — held.
- No advancement of the rehab plan (no move to 40 min, no third run, no extra frequency) — held.

What this is not:
- Not a setback. The 35-min tolerance closed at 6/6 clean on 9/9/27; one lighter day (walk in place of run) doesn't reopen that window, restart the count, or require re-testing.
- Not a third weekly session. It's a substitute for today's planned run, not an addition.
- Not a route substitution that introduces ankle-twisting risk — "flat ordinary" is by description lower-hazard than trail.

Why the wait-and-run option is less conservative here:
- It holds the dose and route constant but doesn't reduce load — it's at-dose, not below-dose. The only change is time of day (shifted to midday or later, ~4+ hours from your 7:20 AM arrival), which adds a minor variable (heat, hydration, time-of-day effect) without reducing ankle demand.

One small note on tomorrow: the following-morning symptom check applies to whatever you do today — walk or run. If the walk is clean and the following morning is clean, the next planned 35-min easy run slot stays open on a nonconsecutive day within the week. If you choose the walk and want the run dose preserved for the week, the other run slot still needs to be used on a nonconsecutive day from today (Sat 9/18), so earliest eligible run day is Mon 9/20 or later.

RETIREMENT INDICATORS — current pair (412 mi logged, 7/17/27)

Already present on the current pair:
  - Midsole creasing deeper than the unworn side (foam compression; cushioning reduced)
  - Outer-rear heel rubber smoothed (grip reduced; mild)
  - Upper still intact (not yet a factor)

Any one of these is enough to retire:
  - New or returning focal ankle / calf / knee / hip symptoms during a run or the following day
  - Creasing turns from soft folds into sharp creases
  - Visible midsole foam "wrinkles" or stack-height loss
  - Heel counter collapse, heel slip, or upper looseness
  - Outsole smooth patches wider than a thumbnail under ball or heel
  - Twist test: shoe folds in half too easily
  - Lateral heel squeeze: heel collapses under light hand pressure
  - Cumulative mileage at or past 450 (current: 412)

Conservative timing call, given the ankle-rehab context:
  - Don't run this pair through 8/19 and beyond. Five more weeks at the current pace lands near 460–480 mi with midsole compression already present — past the conservative line.
  - Plan to retire within the next 1–2 weeks; replace with same-geometry shoe; break in over 1–2 short easy sessions inside the current 30-min cap.
  - Don't defer the purchase until after 8/19 unless the clinic explicitly says otherwise on 8/19.

LIMITS — unchanged through the 8/19/27 reassessment

Running:
  - 2 nonconsecutive 30-minute continuous easy runs/week
  - Easy effort (conversational; no focal symptoms)
  - No third session, no longer duration, no run on a bike-commute day
  - Ankle-and-calf strengthening 3×/week

Bike (temporary):
  - Tuesday and Thursday commute legs only
  - ≤25 minutes per leg, easy effort
  - Not a third run substitute

Stop / roll-back conditions (unchanged):
  - Focal pain, swelling, instability, or gait change during a session
  - Same-day or following-day symptoms outside the planning window

REPLACEMENT-SHOE STORE CHECKLIST

Match what works — change one variable at a time:
  - Neutral daily-trainer category (no stability post, no motion control)
  - Drop near 8 mm; avoid shifts to >10 mm or <6 mm
  - Stack and feel similar to current 9.2 oz
  - Avoid: maximalist rocker, carbon / plated race-day shoes, minimalist / barefoot

Bring:
  - Current pair (to compare last and midfoot geometry)
  - Running socks you actually use
  - Any inserts / orthotics used on runs

In-store fit test:
  - Try on later in the day (foot is larger)
  - Standing fit: thumb-width past longest toe; snug midfoot; locked heel
  - Walk + light jog on hard floor; check heel slip, hot spots, lateral pressure
  - Lacing: lock the heel without over-tightening the forefoot

Structural checks before paying:
  - Twist test: some twist OK for a neutral; should not fold in half
  - Lateral heel squeeze: should resist light hand pressure
  - Outsole texture intact under ball and heel

At the store, do not:
  - Take a "more cushion = better" upsell that changes drop or stack
  - Accept a stability / motion-control suggestion without clinic input
  - Switch brand and model in the same purchase
  - Rotate two new pairs during the rehab window

Break-in, inside current limits:
  - First run in new pair: 15–20 min easy, same surface as recent runs
  - Second run: same as first unless symptoms
  - Then resume the normal 2×/week 30-min pattern in the new pair
  - Keep the current pair until the new pair has 2 clean sessions, in case the new fit fails

Keep on file:
  - Receipt, model + size + width, purchase date, starting mileage
  - Store return policy (most allow runnable returns for 30 days)

NOT in this read:
  - Not a new clearance, not a model recommendation, not a gait analysis
  - Does not authorize any change to running duration or frequency, bike days, bike duration, or bike effort
  - Does not replace the 8/19 reassessment

- Skip the bike commute. An allowed Tue/Thu slot is not authorization to ride when elevated surfaces are slick; surface conditions, not mechanical soundness or ankle status, control the call.

Activation Definition v2 — Glossary Note
==========================================

Purpose
-------
Historical analyses may still reference activation definition v2. This note
documents v2's exact criteria, the window during which it was the live
activation cut, and the standing rule for v2 after its replacement so
analysts, experiments, and reporting all stay consistent.

Exact criteria
--------------
Activation definition v2 is a workspace-level flag with both conditions
required inside a 14-day window from signup:

  1. First integration connected (the workspace wired the integration).
  2. The user logged in at least twice within the same 14-day window.

The login-twice gate is what distinguishes v2 from v1 (which only required
first integration in 14 days) and v3 (which replaces the login-twice gate
with an in-product event requirement).

Period when v2 was the active cut
---------------------------------
Live from: November 2022
Replaced: March 16, 2023, when activation definition v3 was shipped.

From November 2022 through March 16, 2023, v2 was the default activation

Erratum date: 2028-01-01
Owner: Riley
Scope: EXP-2023-02-onboarding-trigger (`lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2`) and the mid-segment read around it, March–April 2023.

This note exists so future readers do not reuse the original cohort logic. Two issues made the original read noisier than it had to be: a classification problem with the cohort boundary, and a timing problem with the trigger itself.

1. Corrected cohort boundary
   - Original (mid-seg v1): 50–200 seat paid accounts. This is what EXP-2023-02 ran on.
   - Corrected (mid-seg v2): 75–200 seat paid accounts. Use this for any new analysis.
   - The 50–75 seat band behaves like starter once retention, expansion, and LTV are compared side by side. Including it in the mid-seg cut was muddying the read (it pulled in starter-shaped accounts that diluted the effect and gave Marcus an easy ugly chart to grab).
   - The old v1 50–200 cut stays in the warehouse / query layer for historical comps because we have used it since Sep 2024. Anything new — including retrospective re-reads of the April 2023 onboarding-trigger data — should be reported under v2 (75–200), with v1 shown alongside only as a comparability row, never as the headline.

2. Classification issue that made the original read noisier
   - The 50–75 seat slice inside the v1 50–200 bucket was the single biggest source of cohort-shape noise in the April 2023 window. It is not a mid-segment behavior; it is starter behavior with a larger seat count.
   - Symptom: signup-source, tier, and geo splits were clean on the dipped cohorts, but the band kept producing ugly charts whenever anyone sliced aggressively. That is a classification artifact, not a trigger artifact.
   - Fix going forward: report mid-segment reads under 75–200. Do not summarize the 50–75 band as "mid-seg expansion pool," "retained mid," or Expansion Assist scope — those are different scopes.

3. Timing issue that made the original read noisier
   - The original `lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2` variant is activation-keyed, not literal-calendar-day-7 keyed. Reading the April 2023 cohorts on a calendar-day-7 window (i.e., treating "day-7" as a wall-clock day from signup) double-counts or mis-cuts accounts whose activation lands inside vs. just after the cutoff, and it leaks in Thu/Fri signup composition effects that show up as apparent trigger wobble.
   - Symptom: the dipped second post-ship cohort had a slightly fatter Thu/Fri signup mix than the cleaner cohorts — that is partly a window-definition artifact once the trigger went 100% on Apr 10, not a real regression in `lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2`.
   - Related timing item worth keeping straight: EXP-2023-02 launched Mar 13, 2023, not Mar 12. Eng review pushed it a day. Any reader reconstructing the test window should anchor on Mar 13; assuming Mar 12 shifts every cohort boundary by one day.

What this changes for retrospective reads of April 2023
   - Recompute under mid-seg v2 (75–200), not v1 (50–200).
   - Recompute the week-1 retention window off the activation-keyed event, not off a literal calendar day-7 from signup.
   - Anchor cohort windows on the Mar 13 launch, not Mar 12.
   - Treat the 50–75 seat band as out-of-scope for mid-segment conclusions, present only as a comparability note if at all.

What this does NOT change
   - The pooled +3.1 pts treatment-vs-control week-1 retention read (p=0.04, n=420 across the two pre-ship cohorts) and the +3.2 first post-ship cohort read are the underlying effect estimates; the boundary and window corrections above change how the cohort is defined and measured, not the underlying treatment.
   - The 100% rollout on Apr 10, 2023 stands. This erratum is about how to read the historical data, not about reversing the ship.
   - EXP-2023-02-onboarding-trigger remains scope-disjoint from `pricing_page_2023q2_rev`. Do not mash attribution across the two.

If you are about to cite the April 2023 onboarding-trigger numbers in a deck, appendix, or board package, stop and re-pull under the corrected boundary and window above. If the source you are copying from does not say "mid-seg v2 (75–200)" and "activation-keyed window," it is stale.

Erratum date: 2028-01-01
Owner: Riley
Scope: EXP-2023-02-onboarding-trigger (`lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2`) and the mid-segment read around it, March–April 2023.

This note exists so future readers do not reuse the original cohort logic. Two issues made the original read noisier than it had to be: a classification problem with the cohort boundary, and a timing problem with the trigger itself.

1. Corrected cohort boundary
   - Original (mid-seg v1): 50–200 seat paid accounts. This is what EXP-2023-02 ran on.
   - Corrected (mid-seg v2): 75–200 seat paid accounts. Use this for any new analysis.
   - The 50–75 seat band behaves like starter once retention, expansion, and LTV are compared side by side. Including it in the mid-seg cut was muddying the read (it pulled in starter-shaped accounts that diluted the effect and gave Marcus an easy ugly chart to grab).
   - The old v1 50–200 cut stays in the warehouse / query layer for historical comps because we have used it since Sep 2024. Anything new — including retrospective re-reads of the April 2023 onboarding-trigger data — should be reported under v2 (75–200), with v1 shown alongside only as a comparability row, never as the headline.

2. Classification issue that made the original read noisier
   - The 50–75 seat slice inside the v1 50–200 bucket was the single biggest source of cohort-shape noise in the April 2023 window. It is not a mid-segment behavior; it is starter behavior with a larger seat count.
   - Symptom: signup-source, tier, and geo splits were clean on the dipped cohorts, but the band kept producing ugly charts whenever anyone sliced aggressively. That is a classification artifact, not a trigger artifact.
   - Fix going forward: report mid-segment reads under 75–200. Do not summarize the 50–75 band as "mid-seg expansion pool," "retained mid," or Expansion Assist scope — those are different scopes.

3. Timing issue that made the original read noisier
   - The original `lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2` variant is activation-keyed, not literal-calendar-day-7 keyed. Reading the April 2023 cohorts on a calendar-day-7 window (i.e., treating "day-7" as a wall-clock day from signup) double-counts or mis-cuts accounts whose activation lands inside vs. just after the cutoff, and it leaks in Thu/Fri signup composition effects that show up as apparent trigger wobble.
   - Symptom: the dipped second post-ship cohort had a slightly fatter Thu/Fri signup mix than the cleaner cohorts — that is partly a window-definition artifact once the trigger went 100% on Apr 10, not a real regression in `lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2`.
   - Related timing item worth keeping straight: EXP-2023-02 launched Mar 13, 2023, not Mar 12. Eng review pushed it a day. Any reader reconstructing the test window should anchor on Mar 13; assuming Mar 12 shifts every cohort boundary by one day.

What this changes for retrospective reads of April 2023
   - Recompute under mid-seg v2 (75–200), not v1 (50–200).
   - Recompute the week-1 retention window off the activation-keyed event, not off a literal calendar day-7 from signup.
   - Anchor cohort windows on the Mar 13 launch, not Mar 12.
   - Treat the 50–75 seat band as out-of-scope for mid-segment conclusions, present only as a comparability note if at all.

What this does NOT change
   - The pooled +3.1 pts treatment-vs-control week-1 retention read (p=0.04, n=420 across the two pre-ship cohorts) and the +3.2 first post-ship cohort read are the underlying effect estimates; the boundary and window corrections above change how the cohort is defined and measured, not the underlying treatment.
   - The 100% rollout on Apr 10, 2023 stands. This erratum is about how to read the historical data, not about reversing the ship.
   - EXP-2023-02-onboarding-trigger remains scope-disjoint from `pricing_page_2023q2_rev`. Do not mash attribution across the two.

If you are about to cite the April 2023 onboarding-trigger numbers in a deck, appendix, or board package, stop and re-pull under the corrected boundary and window above. If the source you are copying from does not say "mid-seg v2 (75–200)" and "activation-keyed window," it is stale.
