Design-lineage note. Two separate threads. Treat them as distinct changes; do not conflate.

================================================================
THREAD 1 — Onboarding email trigger change (pricing-page CTA layout move)
================================================================

What changed
- Released 2027-11-05 ~14:10 CT by Daniela.
- Scope: layout move of the existing "Get setup help" CTA to a position above the pricing-page comparison table on the assisted route.
- Post-period move; the July 1 – October 31 Pricing Path Clarity Test window was already closed and certified before the release, and no pricing-page experiment is running.
- No A/B test, no new touch, no schedule change.

What was deliberately NOT changed (verified at release)
- Wording: "Get setup help".
- Destination: Customer Success assisted path.
- Event key and telemetry: unchanged, recording normally.
- Eligibility, admission, and routing logic: unchanged.
- Rollback behavior: unchanged.
- Owner authority: Daniela retains release and rollback control.

Why this is its own thread
- This is a layout-only change on an existing, already-approved CTA. The underlying consumer, the audience, the copy, the destination, and the instrumentation all carried through unchanged.
- It is the resolution of an earlier semantic question (the rejected "Start setup" replacement proposed 2027-08-14). "Start setup" was never released; "Get setup help" is the in-production wording that moved position.
- Bounded approval conditions: every one of the five unchanged surfaces above was a release-gate check, not a side effect.

Lineage pointers
- Predecessor copy event: 2027-08-26 (copy owner replaced rejected "Start setup" with "Get setup help" on the assisted route); 2027-08-27 (Daniela released that wording).
- Bounded approval: 2027-11-03 (post-period layout move approved with the unchanged-surface conditions).
- Release: 2027-11-05.

================================================================
THREAD 2 — Activation definition review and successor metric direction
================================================================

What was reviewed
- The Helio activation definition that had been live since November 2022, written as: first integration plus two logins within 14 days ("v2").
- Review trigger: v2 was deemed UI-shaped — it credited accounts that hit a login-count gate without verifying the account had actually used the product.
- Specific cohort the review surfaced against: mid-segment users (the 50–200 seat v1 bucket). The Feb 28 H3 cut on calendar-day vs activation-day bucketing for the day-7 email showed a 3.1% vs 7.8% divergence that v2 could not cleanly explain.

Why v2 was reviewed (the substantive reason, not just the trigger)
- v2 was undercounting the exact customers Helio wanted to count: accounts that wired the integration, have data flowing, and never really click around. They cross v2's 2-logins gate without ever producing a product-seen event.
- Conversely, v2 overcounted login-shaped activity as activation even when there was no real product use.
- Net effect: the definition was giving "fake comfort" — top-line activation read high relative to the underlying product proof, particularly in the post-pricing-page wobble period.

Successor metric direction (v3, the intended direction)
- Definition: first integration plus at least one in-product event within 14 days.
- Guardrail shape: "product-seen" rather than "UI-shape". The login count is no longer the gate; an in-product event is.
- Boundary principle: integrate-first with a product-seen guardrail. Not "more events," not "longer window," not "stricter integration." A single in-product event inside the existing 14-day window is the intended successor.
- Operational handling of the transition: v1, v2, and v3 are all retained as versioned tables so historical cohort comps remain auditable. Nothing was deleted; nothing was overwritten in place.

Why v3 was framed as a reanalysis overlay, not a replacement
- The onboarding-trigger A/B (lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2, rolled 2023-03-13) had v2's activation definition baked into its treatment rule (the treatment suppresses day-7 for non-activated mid-segment users).
- Changing the definition mid-run would have made "non-activated" mean a different thing on day 1 vs day 14, making the treatment effect unreadable.
- Chosen sequencing: freeze v2 inside the EXP readout, finish the powered two weeks under v2, then run v3 reanalysis as a separate overlay. Log the v2→v3 transition date in the EXP doc so the readout frame stays honest.
- Consequence: the Feb 28 H3 cut (3.1% / 7.8%) was a v2-bucket assignment and was explicitly rerun under v3; bucket shape changes, not headline churn changes.

Lineage pointers
- Predecessor definitions retained: v1 (Aug 2022) = first integration in 14 days; v2 (Nov 2022) = first integration + 2 logins in 14 days.
- Review session: 2023-03-15 with Owen; v3 drafted as integration-first with product-seen guardrail.
- Implementation: 2023-03-16, versioned tables in the warehouse.
- Successor direction owner: Owen (definition), Riley (lifecycle framing), Ines (lifecycle governance), Daniela (engineering).

================================================================
Explicit distinction — read this before treating them as one change
================================================================

These two threads share two words ("activation" and "onboarding") and nothing else of consequence.

Thread 1 is a layout-only move of an already-approved pricing-page CTA. It touches wording, destination, event key, eligibility, routing, and rollback only to verify they are unchanged. No metric, no definition, no consumer.

Thread 2 is a redefinition of the activation metric itself and the framing of its successor. It changes which accounts count as activated, requires a product-seen event rather than a login count, and is sequenced as an overlay so the in-flight onboarding-trigger A/B stays readable.

If a future reader sees "activation" mentioned in the context of the November 2027 CTA move, that is a coincidence of vocabulary — Thread 1 did not change the activation metric, the activation consumer, or the activation successor direction. The v2→v3 work is its own lineage with its own owners and its own retention policy (versioned, not deleted).

- It is the resolution of an earlier semantic question (the rejected "Start setup" replacement proposed 2027-08-14). "Start setup" was never released; "Get setup help" is the in-production wording that moved position.

================================================================
THREAD 2 — Activation definition review and successor metric direction
================================================================

What was reviewed
- The Helio activation definition that had been live since November 2022, written as: first integration plus two logins within 14 days ("v2").
- Review trigger: v2 was deemed UI-shaped — it credited accounts that hit a login-count gate without verifying the account had actually used the product.
- Specific cohort the review surfaced against: mid-segment users (the 50–200 seat v1 bucket). The Feb 28 H3 cut on calendar-day vs activation-day bucketing for the day-7 email showed a 3.1% vs 7.8% divergence that v2 could not cleanly explain.

Why v2 was reviewed (the substantive reason, not just the trigger)
- v2 was undercounting the exact customers Helio wanted to count: accounts that wired the integration, have data flowing, and never really click around. They cross v2's 2-logins gate without ever producing a product-seen event.
- Conversely, v2 overcounted login-shaped activity as activation even when there was no real product use.
- Net effect: the definition was giving "fake comfort" — top-line activation read high relative to the underlying product proof, particularly in the post-pricing-page wobble period.

Successor metric direction (v3, the intended direction)
- Definition: first integration plus at least one in-product event within 14 days.
- Guardrail shape: "product-seen" rather than "UI-shape". The login count is no longer the gate; an in-product event is.
- Boundary principle: integrate-first with a product-seen guardrail. Not "more events," not "longer window," not "stricter integration." A single in-product event inside the existing 14-day window is the intended successor.
- Operational handling of the transition: v1, v2, and v3 are all retained as versioned tables so historical cohort comps remain auditable. Nothing was deleted; nothing was overwritten in place.

Why v3 was framed as a reanalysis overlay, not a replacement
- The onboarding-trigger A/B (lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2, rolled 2023-03-13) had v2's activation definition baked into its treatment rule (the treatment suppresses day-7 for non-activated mid-segment users).
- Changing the definition mid-run would have made "non-activated" mean a different thing on day 1 vs day 14, making the treatment effect unreadable.
- Chosen sequencing: freeze v2 inside the EXP readout, finish the powered two weeks under v2, then run v3 reanalysis as a separate overlay. Log the v2→v3 transition date in the EXP doc so the readout frame stays honest.
- Consequence: the Feb 28 H3 cut (3.1% / 7.8%) was a v2-bucket assignment and was explicitly rerun under v3; bucket shape changes, not headline churn changes.

Lineage pointers
- Predecessor definitions retained: v1 (Aug 2022) = first integration in 14 days; v2 (Nov 2022) = first integration + 2 logins in 14 days.
- Review session: 2023-03-15 with Owen; v3 drafted as integration-first with product-seen guardrail.
- Implementation: 2023-03-16, versioned tables in the warehouse.
- Successor direction owner: Owen (definition), Riley (lifecycle framing), Ines (lifecycle governance), Daniela (engineering).

================================================================
Explicit distinction — read this before treating them as one change
================================================================

These two threads share two words ("activation" and "onboarding") and nothing else of consequence.

Thread 1 is a layout-only move of an already-approved pricing-page CTA. It touches wording, destination, event key, eligibility, routing, and rollback only to verify they are unchanged. No metric, no definition, no consumer.

Thread 2 is a redefinition of the activation metric itself and the framing of its successor. It changes which accounts count as activated, requires a product-seen event rather than a login count, and is sequenced as an overlay so the in-flight onboarding-trigger A/B stays readable.

If a future reader sees "activation" mentioned in the context of the November 2027 CTA move, that is a coincidence of vocabulary — Thread 1 did not change the activation metric, the activation consumer, or the activation successor direction. The v2→v3 work is its own lineage with its own owners and its own retention policy (versioned, not deleted).

# July 2023 decision rights — Helio Start and retained-mid expansion

**Period-specific historical record.** Documents the decision-rights posture for July 2023 only. Not current org policy, not present-day ownership, not authoritative for any later action. Where later decisions altered the posture, those changes are out of scope for this entry.

## Period and scope
Two workstreams: **Helio Start** (sub-50-seat self-serve motion) and **Expansion Assist** (retained-mid v2 expansion-design work). Excludes prior framing and any post-July gating decisions.

## Helio Start — July 2023

**Strategic lane**
- Posture on record (June 28 framing held through July): guarded pre-discovery. Not a launch path, beta, pricing-page experiment, or Q3 revenue commitment.
- Gating sequence: eligibility/refusal before packaging; event taxonomy and entitlement instrumentation before any pricing-page experiment; lifecycle fork before any paid acquisition; activation measurement kept separate from retained-mid v2.
- Authority: framing, gating order, and scope limits held at Priya with Riley as operating partner; engineering-gate ownership (instrumentation, lifecycle, support) with Tomás. Marcus (Sales/Growth) explicitly out of any Q3 revenue interpretation.
- Late-July clarification (July 26): a lifecycle-fork update did not unlock the beta path. State-changing lifecycle touches, entitlement/support-state resolution, and pricing-page exposure remained out for July.

**Execution lane** (under the gates above)
- Eligibility and refusal copy: Ines. Substance kept; language reframed from "bad fit" toward customer-protective framing of migration help, agency-shared admin permissions, manual billing exceptions, and heavy support needs routing out.
- Entitlement instrumentation and event taxonomy: Daniela. Plumbing for admin complexity, import/migration help, support handoff, and entitlement state.
- Discovery evidence: 11 rows field-complete for discovery conversations; 6 assisted/refusal-risk; 1 stale (not usable).

## Expansion Assist (retained-mid v2) — July 2023

**Strategic lane**
- Posture: design-phase work only. Not a commercial launch, Sales-ready queue, pipeline source, forecast lever, or revenue-credit source.
- Working scope: prompt-state model, suppression rules, and CS-handoff design for retained-mid v2, intended to constrain the prior day-60 nudge model.
- Authority: framing, eligibility criteria, and CS-handoff boundary held at Priya with Riley as operating partner. Marcus excluded from pipeline/forecast framing of any July output.

**Execution lane** (under the gates above)
- Prompt-state and suppression-rules design: Growth/Owen. Eligibility required active-admin behavior and product-visible usage-ceiling evidence together (usage ceiling alone insufficient). Open CS adoption or renewal work suppressed commercial prompts.
- CS-handoff design: Customer Success. Handoff only on help request or crossed usage ceiling; no automatic Sales-routing.
- Reporting separation: Expansion Assist outputs kept separate from Helio Start activation/support-load and from retained-mid v2 base measurement.

## Lane boundary (July 2023)
- **Strategic** (framing, gating, scope, exclusions, credit/forecast status): Priya, with Riley as operating partner. Engineering-gate ownership on Helio Start with Tomás.
- **Execution** (copy, instrumentation, taxonomy, prompt-state design, CS-handoff design): Daniela, Ines, Owen, Customer Success — within the strategic gates above.
- **Out of lane**: Marcus Vail for Q3 revenue interpretation of Helio Start, and for any pipeline/forecast credit on Expansion Assist.

## Labeling
This is a July 2023 record only. Later changes — including the bounded July 2024 Expansion Assist pilot, the March 2024 Helio Start GA, and the Q1 2026 organic-channel extension — are explicitly out of scope for this entry and described elsewhere in the governance record.

**Period-specific historical record.** Documents the decision-rights posture for July 2023 only. Not current org policy, not present-day ownership, not authoritative for any later action. Where later decisions altered the posture, those changes are out of scope for this entry.

## Period and scope
Two workstreams: **Helio Start** (sub-50-seat self-serve motion) and **Expansion Assist** (retained-mid v2 expansion-design work). Excludes prior framing and any post-July gating decisions.

## Helio Start — July 2023

**Strategic lane**
- Posture on record (June 28 framing held through July): guarded pre-discovery. Not a launch path, beta, pricing-page experiment, or Q3 revenue commitment.
- Gating sequence: eligibility/refusal before packaging; event taxonomy and entitlement instrumentation before any pricing-page experiment; lifecycle fork before any paid acquisition; activation measurement kept separate from retained-mid v2.
- Authority: framing, gating order, and scope limits held at Priya with Riley as operating partner; engineering-gate ownership (instrumentation, lifecycle, support) with Tomás. Marcus (Sales/Growth) explicitly out of any Q3 revenue interpretation.
- Late-July clarification (July 26): a lifecycle-fork update did not unlock the beta path. State-changing lifecycle touches, entitlement/support-state resolution, and pricing-page exposure remained out for July.

**Execution lane** (under the gates above)
- Eligibility and refusal copy: Ines. Substance kept; language reframed from "bad fit" toward customer-protective framing of migration help, agency-shared admin permissions, manual billing exceptions, and heavy support needs routing out.
- Entitlement instrumentation and event taxonomy: Daniela. Plumbing for admin complexity, import/migration help, support handoff, and entitlement state.
- Discovery evidence: 11 rows field-complete for discovery conversations; 6 assisted/refusal-risk; 1 stale (not usable).

## Expansion Assist (retained-mid v2) — July 2023

**Strategic lane**
- Posture: design-phase work only. Not a commercial launch, Sales-ready queue, pipeline source, forecast lever, or revenue-credit source.
- Working scope: prompt-state model, suppression rules, and CS-handoff design for retained-mid v2, intended to constrain the prior day-60 nudge model.
- Authority: framing, eligibility criteria, and CS-handoff boundary held at Priya with Riley as operating partner. Marcus excluded from pipeline/forecast framing of any July output.

**Execution lane** (under the gates above)
- Prompt-state and suppression-rules design: Growth/Owen. Eligibility required active-admin behavior and product-visible usage-ceiling evidence together (usage ceiling alone insufficient). Open CS adoption or renewal work suppressed commercial prompts.
- CS-handoff design: Customer Success. Handoff only on help request or crossed usage ceiling; no automatic Sales-routing.
- Reporting separation: Expansion Assist outputs kept separate from Helio Start activation/support-load and from retained-mid v2 base measurement.

## Lane boundary (July 2023)
- **Strategic** (framing, gating, scope, exclusions, credit/forecast status): Priya, with Riley as operating partner. Engineering-gate ownership on Helio Start with Tomás.
- **Execution** (copy, instrumentation, taxonomy, prompt-state design, CS-handoff design): Daniela, Ines, Owen, Customer Success — within the strategic gates above.
- **Out of lane**: Marcus Vail for Q3 revenue interpretation of Helio Start, and for any pipeline/forecast credit on Expansion Assist.

## Labeling
This is a July 2023 record only. Later changes — including the bounded July 2024 Expansion Assist pilot, the March 2024 Helio Start GA, and the Q1 2026 organic-channel extension — are explicitly out of scope for this entry and described elsewhere in the governance record.

## 2025-09-12 — Finalist evidence, reference-check sequencing, and open questions (additive; selection remains open)

This is an additive update. The brief body is not replaced. No hiring decision is made or implied. Selection remains open until references return and are reviewed.

### 1. Finalist status (first-round evidence, Sept 3–5)

- **Candidate A (Sept 3, 3:00–3:30 PM CT) — advances.**
  Evidence: produced a concrete audit-traceability example (not abstract); explicitly separated evidence preparation from approval during the interview, consistent with the bounded prep-capacity role; proposed a credible Customer.io learning plan. Fits the 30-day bounded scope.

- **Candidate B (Sept 4, 11:00–11:30 AM CT) — does not advance.**
  Evidence: deepest lifecycle-tool experience of the three, but repeatedly described routine review as something the contractor would eventually sign off on, despite restated scope limits. The authority mismatch is structural, not a presentation slip — it cannot be remediated within the bounded prep-capacity role and would conflict with the established owner lanes (Owen routine; Ines messaging + lifecycle governance; Daniela transport + source reliability; Riley high-stakes only).

- **Candidate C (Sept 5, 2:00–2:30 PM CT) — advances.**
  Evidence: produced concrete handoff-map and campaign-inventory examples; respected owner lanes without prompting. Fits the 30-day bounded scope. Needed prompting on denominator checks and rework measurement during the interview.

**Finalists: A and C.** Per Procurement, two finalist interviews are scheduled. Selection is open. No contractor has been selected.

### 2. Evidence-based reference-check priority (sequencing, not selection)

Criterion: the finalist whose residual gap maps onto a harder-to-remediate scope-safety floor carries higher decision leverage through references — i.e., the reference most likely to materially change the call if it returns a specific signal.

- **Priority 1 — Candidate C.**
  Residual gap: denominator discipline and rework measurement.
  Why this ranks first: this gap maps directly onto two of the four 60-day guardrails already specified for the role (rework; boundary integrity, per the Aug 28 finance frame) and is harder to remediate through ramp-up training than a tooling-learning gap. It is also less observable from a single interview than traceability examples. References should test whether C has actually practiced this discipline under volume — behavioral, not abstract.

- **Priority 2 — Candidate A.**
  Residual gap: scaling traceability beyond a single example; Customer.io ramp.
  Why this ranks second: more remediable through the structured Customer.io learning plan and a first-two-week ramp. References should test scale-volume behavior and the ability to learn a new tool under deadline.

This ranking sequences reference depth and promptness. It is not a preference signal. Both finalists remain in consideration. Either could be eliminated by reference returns; neither is pre-decided.

### 3. Remaining questions (open before references return and before any decision)

1. **Reference return timing.** Actual dates from each reference contact, not assumed. Alignment target — Sept 16 rehearsal, Sept 19 lock, Sept 24 decision, or independent of those dates?
2. **Finalist interview agenda.** Bounded probes for each finalist, distinct per residual gap (denominator/rework for C; scale/tooling-ramp for A). Shared probe for both: stale fields, holds, disputed semantics, message governance, rollback boundaries, high-stakes language, scope exclusions.
3. **Reference depth.** How many references per finalist? Direct manager required? Cross-functional required? Former client/PMO?
4. **Decision authority and threshold.** Who signs the final call — Riley alone, or does the Procurement / hiring-packet process require additional sign-off?
5. **Onboarding prerequisites.** Day-1 access list — Owen (ledger), Daniela (transport/source), Ines (messaging/governance), Customer.io sandbox.
6. **Backout path.** If references surface a material concern for one finalist, is the other the default, or do we re-open the pipeline?
7. **Start date alignment.** Oct-start readiness sequencing — when does the contractor actually begin, and is that date contingent on the Sept 24 decision or independent?
8. **Order of finalist interviews vs. references.** Sequential (interviews then references), interleaved, or parallel?
9. **Reference scoring rubric.** What counts as a "pass" reference — specific behavioral scenarios tied to each finalist's residual gap, or general competency/character?
10. **Scope guardrails on hire.** Confirm in writing that neither finalist, on hire, receives semantic, review-closure, lifecycle-release, exception, or engineering-control authority. The role is preparation capacity only.

### 4. What this update is not

- Not a hiring decision. Selection remains open.
- Not a preference signal between finalists. The reference-check priority is sequencing, not ranking-for-selection.
- Not a downgrade of Candidate B's experience. B's experience is real; the authority mismatch is the disqualifier, and it is structural.
- Not a guarantee that either finalist will pass references.
- Not an expansion of the role scope. The bounded 30-day scope (inventory + audit calendar + owner-signed handoff map) and the 60-day guardrails stand as previously framed.
- Not a change to established owner lanes (Owen, Ines, Daniela, Riley).

The praise should point to three specific things: he separated the 30-application intake evidence from the 22-workspace outcome evidence before the Helio Start executive review, he reconciled the duplicate Start submission without changing the other 23 applications, and he replaced the misleading 4.6-point activation headline with a mix-standardized read. **Strengths / keep doing**

Owen's strongest analytical work this month has been three judgment calls that materially improved the readiness and onboarding reads. Before the Helio Start executive review, he separated the 30-application intake evidence from the 22-workspace outcome evidence and kept them in distinct panels, so intake classification and post-acceptance outcomes no longer shared a denominator. When a duplicate Start submission arrived through the waitlist and a referral 17 minutes apart, he reconciled it by counting the company once, retaining both provenance signals, and leaving the other 23 applications untouched. And when the 4.6-point crude activation headline was being repeated in the operating review without the cohort-mix sentence that followed it, he replaced it with a mix-standardized read that leads with composition and denominators and makes explicit that there is no causal or ship claim. In each case the underlying numbers stayed unchanged; what changed was the framing. That is the standard I want him to keep working at.

**Growth area**

The growth area is about when Owen surfaces analytical risk, not what he does about it. He has a pattern of quietly repairing ambiguous scope, denominator, or causal assumptions in his own work — fixing the 52-record pool, fixing the duplicate, fixing the crude-activation headline — and only raising the risk once the corrected version is nearly ready. The repairs themselves are good. The cost is that the rest of us, including me, find out about the problem at the same moment we see the fix, which compresses the time we have to weigh in on what the corrected version should say. Earlier flagging — even a one-line note like "I think the denominator here is mixing two things, going to separate before I share" — would let the team react to the diagnosis, not just the conclusion. Speed is not the issue; the timing of the surfacing is.

messages.content: [2023-09-14T08:20:00-05:00] Priya asked me to join a thirty-minute Growth Ops Analyst interview on Friday, September 15 at 1:00pm Central. The candidate is still unnamed in my notes. Their take-home was promising on cohort instinct but wobbly on causal claims and audience quality. I do not need a full interview script; I want six focused questions that tell me whether they can handle messy growth analysis without over-sending lifecycle email or overclaiming from thin data.

Six questions, each aimed at a specific failure mode. I've put a "what I'm listening for" under each — that's what I'd actually be scoring on.

1. The mid-segment cohort was redefined from 50–200 to 75–200 in late April because 50–75 looked starter on retention, expansion, and LTV. The old v1 definition is preserved for historical comparison; new analyses use v2. Someone hands you a retention chart that crosses the boundary — v1 on the left, v2 on the right, no label change. Walk me through what you'd do before you trust or share that chart.
   Listen for: do they ask about version boundaries before they ask about the metric? Do they want both definitions preserved, or do they want to "clean it up"? A good answer treats v1 vs v2 as a first-class distinction; a weak answer reaches for a chart redesign before questioning the cut.

2. You have a snapshot that shows users activated before day 7 churned at 3.1% versus 7.8% for users not activated by day 7, n=210. Marcus wants a lifecycle email at activation. What do you actually do with that number before recommending anything?
   Listen for: do they name the selection problem — activated-by-day-7 is correlated with account type, intent, and admin engagement, not just the act of activating? Do they distinguish direction from evidence? Do they propose an A/B to test the timing claim rather than recommend a send based on the observational gap? A weak answer builds the email off the gap; a strong answer treats the gap as a hypothesis to test.

3. We're running an A/B on the onboarding email timing. Two weeks in, someone proposes a "quick read" by comparing the treated cohort's week-one retention against last quarter's pre-experiment baseline. What's wrong with that, and what would you do instead?
   Listen for: do they immediately name the confound (cohort mix, seasonality, any shipped changes in the window)? Do they refuse the pre/post shortcut and push for a within-window treatment vs control cut? Bonus if they ask whether anything shipped mid-experiment that should be held constant.

4. We're planning a tip digest for retained-account workspace admins. Customer.io has two role fields — `current_role` and a cached snapshot from first integration. The cached field is what's been used on prior sends; `current_role` was added later. Walk me through how you'd build and validate the audience, including what you'd explicitly exclude.
   Listen for: do they default to `current_role` and treat the cached field as a known-bad default? Do they list concrete exclusions — suspended workspaces, viewer-only contacts, hard-bounced addresses, unsubscribes? Do they ask for a diff against the last send's audience, not just a count? A weak answer says "use the role field" without naming which one; a strong answer treats the role-field choice as the whole question.

5. A beta cohort shows first-integration rates landing in the expected early window. Simultaneously, support tickets per active beta account are spiking, concentrated in permissions/admin-role confusion, CSV import expectations, and billing expectation mismatches. Marcus wants to call activation "on track." How do you read these together, and what does the read let you say?
   Listen for: do they refuse to call activation on track without the support signal beside it? Do they keep the support categories distinct rather than collapsing to "onboarding friction"? Do they distinguish learning and support load from launch readiness and from revenue? A weak answer treats activation as the headline; a strong answer makes the support distribution the constraint.

6. We ran a 14-day expansion-nudge readout at n=89 with a +$4/account lift. Marcus wants to call it a win and widen to 50%. The original bar was +$8. What do you say, and what additional cuts would you want before any decision?
   Listen for: do they name the n, the bar, and the underpowered window before they name the lift? Do they refuse the widen call and ask for either a powered window…

Scope note: design input for retained-mid review only. Not a broad prompt, not a Q3 forecast lever. Audience: retained mid-segment v2 (75–200-seat paid) accounts that have already been through lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2. No Helio Start or pricing-page linkage.

Working states

1. Suppress — account not ready
   Trigger when any of the following hold:
   - Insufficient integration depth (e.g., <3 integrations live by day 45, or no first-integration event in window).
   - Inactive admin behavior (no active admin in last 14 days, or admin-only seats without login motion).
   - An open Sales or CS motion on the account (renewal, save, expansion conversation already in flight).
   Behavior: do not prompt. Hold for re-evaluation at the next readiness check.

2. Educate — readiness behavior present, no handoff needed
   Trigger when integration depth + active-admin behavior are present AND there is no commercial signal:
   - Integration depth: 3+ integrations live, recent data flow, no stale-only setup.
   - Active-admin behavior: 2+ admins with login activity in last 14 days, or a single active admin with clear ownership.
   - No open Sales/CS motion, no usage-ceiling pattern, no pricing-page visit, no explicit commercial ask.
   Behavior: in-product education touch only (usage tips, deeper feature awareness). No prompt, no handoff.

3. Alert Sales
   Trigger when the account shows commercial-conversation evidence — active-admin behavior AND usage-ceiling evidence together. Neither alone qualifies.
   - Active-admin behavior: 2+ admins with login activity in the last 14 days, or a single admin with clear ownership AND recent activity. Seat count alone or retained-mid status alone do not qualify.
   - Usage-ceiling evidence: repeated near-limit signals on seat count, integration count, or rate limits; an active admin asking about higher tiers, contracts, or seat expansion via in-product or support; or a pricing-page visit from a known retained-mid admin in the same window.
   - No open adoption work on the account (see Hand off to CS). Adoption work preempts any Sales alert.
   Behavior: route to Sales with a short context note (active-admin signal, ceiling signal, integration depth). Sales owns the conversation; Growth does not prompt.

4. Hand off to CS
   Trigger when adoption help is needed on the account. This state runs FIRST, before any commercial prompt, regardless of whether usage-ceiling evidence is also present on the same account.
   - Permissions/admin-role confusion, missing admin ownership, or setup stalls.
   - Import/migration or manual billing exception in play (routed out of self-serve per existing rules).
   - Support thread already open with unresolved setup or adoption blockers.
   Behavior: CS owns the account. Suppress all commercial prompts and Sales alerts until CS closes the adoption issue and the account returns to a clean readiness state. Usage-ceiling evidence on an adoption-open account does NOT trigger Alert Sales; CS adoption preempts Sales.

5. Suppress collision
   Trigger when a prompt or handoff would collide with an active motion, OR when adoption work is open alongside any commercial signal:
   - Open Sales opportunity, active renewal/save, or pricing-page-active conversation.
   - Open CS adoption thread, migration/import in flight, or manual billing exception being negotiated.
   - Account is in a protected lifecycle window (recent onboarding event, hold per CS request).
   - Stacking rule: when both a Sales motion and an open CS adoption thread are present, CS adoption preempts. The account sits in Suppress collision until CS closes and any Sales motion is re-evaluated against a clean readiness state.
   Behavior: suppress the prompt and any handoff entirely until the collision clears. Re-evaluate at the next readiness check.

False-positive review loop (in-draft, lightweight — not a formal process)
- Cadence: ad-hoc, triggered when a state is misclassified (prompt fires when it should have suppressed, handoff is missed, or the CS-first rule was bypassed) OR when Marcus or CS flags a recurring pattern.
- Reviewers: Owen (analytics), Ines (lifecycle), with Riley joining when a pattern touches Expansion Assist scope.
- Surface: a short log entry under "False-positive log" in this working draft — date, account pseudonym, observed state vs. expected state, why it was wrong, what to change. No QA queue, no SLA, no escalation path.
- Purpose: capture patterns we can learn from while the matrix is still in design mode. The loop exists to inform revisions of the working states; it does not turn the matrix into a launch spec, a Q3 lever, or a formal Growth process. If the loop starts to look like one, we collapse it back to the open-question form.

False-positive log
- (empty — populated as misclassifications come in.)

Open questions

- Source of truth: which system owns each input signal (PostHog for behavior, Salesforce/HubSpot for Sales motion, CS tooling for open threads)? Where does the state get computed, and what is the refresh cadence?
- Suppress-window length: how long does a Suppress — account not ready or Suppress collision state hold before re-evaluation? Fixed days, behavior-gated, or tied to the next readiness check?
- Is the in-draft false-positive review loop surfacing patterns that need broader design changes (or is it staying quiet because the matrix is too narrow)? — replaces the prior "who reviews false positives" question; revisits only if the loop starts to look like a formal process.

## Design review decision — 2023-09-14

Scope of this matrix (room agreement)
- Working decision aid for retained-mid v2 / 75–200-seat paid-account review only.
- Not a launch spec, not a forecast lever, not a formal Growth process.
- Does not authorize a broad prompt, a rollout, or any change to the Helio Start controlled beta or pricing page.
- Stays behavior-based and consultative in voice. Owen and Ines's matrix remains the working shape.

Alert Sales — narrowed trigger (Marcus Vail)
- Marcus is OK with an Alert Sales state only when it is tied to real usage-ceiling behavior.
- Active admin on a retained-mid account is not enough by itself. The trigger needs a usage-ceiling signal on top of the behavior-based readiness inputs (integration depth + active-admin behavior) — e.g., repeated near-limit behavior on seats, integrations, or rate limits; an admin asking about higher tiers, contracts, or seat expansion; or a pricing-page visit from a known retained-mid admin in the same window.
- Without a usage-ceiling signal, the account stays in Educate or Suppress. Sales does not get alerted on general "active admin" retention.

Collision rule — sharpened per CS
- Any open adoption work on the account must suppress or route to CS before any Sales routing happens.
- Open adoption work includes: permissions/admin-role confusion, missing admin ownership, setup stalls, import/migration in flight, manual billing exception being negotiated, or an unresolved support thread on setup/adoption.
- When adoption work is open, the account is in Hand off to CS. No commercial prompt, no Sales alert, regardless of usage-ceiling behavior. Once CS closes the adoption issue and the account returns to a clean readiness state, the normal Alert Sales rules re-apply.
- Suppress collision now explicitly stacks: open Sales motion + open CS adoption work both force Suppress collision; CS adoption takes precedence over Sales alert when both are in play.

Implications for the working states
- Alert Sales trigger: usage-ceiling behavior + readiness behavior, AND no open adoption work. Active admin alone does not qualify.
- Hand off to CS: expanded to explicitly preempt Alert Sales when adoption work is open.
- Suppress collision: tightened to require CS adoption review before re-evaluating any commercial path.

Out of scope for this decision
- No change to the Educate state, the Suppress — account not ready state, or the open questions on source of truth, suppress-window length, or false-positive review.
- No expansion of audience, no timing commitment for a rollout, no change to Expansion Assist's status in the QBR appendix or any external narrative.

# Expansion Assist Pilot Measurement Brief

Status: Design-only, bounded pilot. Observational evidence only — not causal evidence, not forecast credit.

---

## 1. Purpose

This brief defines the design, exposure rules, and measurement plan for the Expansion Assist pilot on the retained mid-segment (75–200-seat paid accounts that have already passed `lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2`). It is the working measurement doc for the pilot; it does not authorize rollout, forecast credit, pipeline input, or revenue claim.

What this brief IS NOT: a launch plan, a forecast, a pipeline input, a causal claim, or evidence that Expansion Assist produces lift. Any Expansion Assist readout stays separate from Q3/Q4 revenue lines and from Helio Start reporting.

---

## 2. Locked Pilot Structure (unchanged)

- **Primary cohort:** 30 retained-mid accounts. Intent-to-treat denominator stays at 30. This is the locked primary number.
- **Reserve handling:** Reserves may fill scheduled slots only when the original exposure week arrives, in randomized order. Actual exposures — not assignments — count toward the weekly cap. Reserve exposures are tracked separately and cannot be cited as primary evidence.
- **Weekly capacity cap:** 5 accounts per week (exposures, not assignments).
- **Assignment-visibility controls:** Owen sees the full randomized assignment file; the designated, named Customer Success operations lead sees only the next 7 days of assignments; a frontline test user cannot see future assignments and receives only the account scheduled within 24 hours. Pre-exposure labels are neutral. A weekly access log is maintained. (Verified 2024-05-30; passed.)
- **Intent-to-treat:** Primary denominator is 30 (locked), regardless of eligibility loss, exposure timing, or reserve substitution.
- **Earliest-live boundary:** July 8, 2024. No live prompt may be sent before July 8, 2024.

---

## 3. Shadow-Review Evidence (closed 6-month review, 2024-06-12)

### 3.1 Population

- **Shadow review population:** 240 retained mid-segment accounts reviewed during a closed 6-month Q4-shadow window ending 2024-06-12 (08:50 CT).
- **Flagged subset:** 46 of the 240 accounts showed all three behavior signals: deeper integration use, recent active-admin behavior, and a product-visible usage ceiling.
- **Non-flagged subset:** 194 accounts (240 − 46) that did not meet all three signals.

### 3.2 Subsequent expansion within 45 days (observational, not causal)

- **Flagged subset (n = 46):** 17 accounts expanded within the following 45 days. Expansion rate: 17 / 46 = 36.96% (≈ 37.0%).
- **Non-flagged subset (n = 194):** 11 accounts expanded within the following 45 days. Expansion rate: 11 / 194 = 5.67% (≈ 5.7%).
- **Relative difference:** (36.96% − 5.67%) / 5.67% ≈ 5.52× flagged vs. non-flagged expansion rate (absolute gap ≈ 31.3 percentage points).

### 3.3 Suppression within the flagged subset

- **CS-suppressed (active adoption or renewal work):** 9 of the 46 flagged accounts had active Customer Success adoption or renewal work in flight and would be suppressed from any commercial prompt.
- **Net prompt-eligible flagged pool:** 46 − 9 = 37 accounts.

### 3.4 Interpretive status (explicit)

The shadow association is **observational, not causal evidence, and not forecast credit.** Accounts were not randomized and were not prompted. The counts above describe which accounts happened to share the three signals and whether they expanded in the following 45 days — they do not establish that prompting these accounts would reproduce the rate, that Expansion Assist causes expansion, or that the rate generalizes beyond the shadow window. The shadow review is internal QA evidence for the readiness heuristic, not a treatment-effect estimate.

---

## 4. Eligibility Design Rules

### 4.1 Behavior signals required for "ready to consider"

An account must show all three signals to be considered for Expansion Assist exposure:

1. **Deeper integration use** — sustained, meaningful integration usage (not just a one-time connect).
2. **Recent active-admin behavior** — admin activity that is current, not stale.
3. **Product-visible usage ceiling** — a usage signal product can see (not inferred from off-product signals).

Directional usage-ceiling examples remain acceptable only when clearly labeled.

### 4.2 Suppression rule (state-based, not age-based)

An account that meets all three signals is **suppressed from any commercial prompt** if it has:

- **Active Customer Success adoption work in flight, OR**
- **Active Customer Success renewal work in flight.**

This is a current-state rule, not a fixed signup-age rule.

### 4.3 Copy / framing requirement

The day-60 message uses **current-state copy** — referencing integration depth, recent admin activity, and the product-visible usage ceiling when those signals are present — **not a fixed signup-age anchor.** Eligibility is governed by account state, not tenure.

---

## 5. Preserved Pilot Constraints (unchanged)

- Primary 30-account cohort, separate reserve handling, 5-account weekly exposure cap, assignment-visibility controls, intent-to-treat analysis, and July 8, 2024 earliest-live boundary are all preserved.
- Shadow review remains internal QA evidence — observational, not causal, not forecast credit.
- Expansion Assist remains design-only and stays separate from forecast, pipeline, revenue, and Helio Start reporting.

---

## 6. What This Brief Does Not Claim

- No causal effect of Expansion Assist on expansion.
- No forecast or pipeline input from Expansion Assist.
- No revenue attribution to Expansion Assist.
- No rollout authorization from the shadow counts alone.
- No generalization of the shadow-window rate beyond the reviewed 240 accounts.

Counts in §3 describe the shadow review's observed composition and subsequent-expansion distribution only.

arguments.body:
# Helio Start high-effort blocker diagnostic

## Scope and hypothesis

Restated: within the eight high-effort workspaces, the customer-side access-or-authority vs. product-guidance split is associated with directionally longer elapsed resolution time and more repeat contacts per workspace; the single mixed data-import case sits between the two groups on both reads.

This is a small-sample, descriptive diagnostic. It is not a comparative trial, not an outcome study, and not a basis for any operating decision beyond the next mechanism-level review.

## Cohort frame

- Eight high-effort Helio Start workspaces, accounting for 472 of 684 validated post-admission product-support minutes. The other 13 contacted workspaces account for the remaining 212 minutes and stay outside this diagnostic.
- The accepted 52-workspace cohort and its day-90 statuses are retained as the surrounding frame only. They are not being restated or revised here.
- Exclusions: pre-admission connector-authority assistance and billing contacts. These remain excluded from the post-admission minute counts and from the per-workspace reads.

## Finalized repeat-contact rule

Owen and Customer Success completed QA on the per-workspace contact lists. The agreed rule:

- Exclude system acknowledgements. Automated case-system receipts, ticket-created notices, and routing-confirmation messages are not contacts.
- Count a repeat contact only when a customer or agent adds a new substantive contact after the initial case entry. Substantive = a new message, call, or note that materially advances or reopens the case, not a status ping or template reply.

Two events QA flagged as possible automated acknowledgements — one in the customer-side access-or-authority group, one in the product-guidance group — were confirmed as automated acknowledgements and excluded. The post-QA per-class repeat totals below reflect this disposition.

## Finalized post-QA reads (descriptive)

| Blocker class | Workspaces | Post-admission support minutes | Median resolution (business days) | Repeat contacts (post-QA) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Customer-side access or authority | 4 | 238 | 4.0 | 8 |
| Product guidance | 3 | 174 | 1.6 | 4 |
| Mixed data-import | 1 | 60 | 2.7 | 3 |
| All eight workspaces | 8 | 472 | — | 15 |

Per-class medians are reported because per-workspace n is small (4, 3, 1) and per-workspace resolution times within a class span roughly 2.9–5.2 business days in the authority group and 1.3–2.0 in the product-guidance group; medians describe center without flattening that spread.

Directional shape only: the authority group shows both longer median resolution (4.0 vs. 1.6 business days) and more repeat contacts per workspace (2.0 vs. ~1.3 mean across the eight) than the product-guidance group. The single mixed data-import case (2.7 business days, 3 repeat contacts) sits between the two.

QA disposition: both flagged events were automated acknowledgements and are excluded from the repeat totals above. No other contact was reclassified.

## What this is not

- Not a basis for staffing decisions. The eight-workspace sample is too small and too non-representative to inform support headcount, shift coverage, or CS capacity planning.
- Not a CAC, paid-channel, or paid-acquisition input. Repeat contacts inside an admitted Helio Start cohort are not acquisition-cost evidence and do not justify any paid-channel change.
- Not a basis for broad onboarding redesign. The eight workspaces are the high-effort tail, not a representative slice of Helio Start onboarding; treating them as typical would overstate product-side friction.
- Not a rewrite of any surrounding measure. The day-30 settled-first-cash count (41 of 52), the day-90 status cut (26 paid-active / 4 pre-day-90 cancel / 3 past due / 1 billing hold on the 34 complete windows; 18 immature), the boundary-sensitivity panel, the auth vs. settle boundary, the assisted-routing panel, and the day-92 cancellation remain unchanged.
- Not an Expansion Assist, GA, pricing-page, pipeline, revenue, or forecast read. Same boundary language as the day-90 cut and the Helio Start continuation gate.
- Not causal. The class split is associated with longer resolution and more repeats in this sample; that is a description of these eight workspaces, not a treatment effect on Helio Start as a whole.

## Open questions for the next review (descriptive)

- Per-class elapsed-time distribution and repeat-contact spread, not just medians, so the within-class variance stays visible.
- Whether the one mixed data-import case generalizes or stays a single workspace.
- Whether the authority-group pattern repeats in the next window of post-admission contacts (separate diagnostic, not folded into this brief).
- Whether any of the eight workspaces cleared on resubmission vs. on a different contact path; recorded separately, not used to revise the repeat totals above.

## Status

Descriptive diagnostic. Mechanism-level review complete for these eight. Not open-ended; the next read is the next mechanism-level pass, not a Helio Start continuation decision.

messages.content:
Saved at 2,164/2,200. Now the draft — concise, internal, four-gate reaffirmation, fail-closed.

---

**Subject:** Re: incomplete-setup reminder audience — staying within current scope

Growth — thanks for raising this. I want to keep the reminder exactly where it's been approved and not move it today.

The reminder remains limited to **a qualifying human admin**, evaluated against **current** entitlement. That scope is not a workaround we can soften — it's the boundary the existing release sits inside. Expanding it would constitute a new consumer of the shared-state feed, and no sixth consumer is authorized.

Two operational gates already sit on every evaluation:

- **Suppressed when active Customer Success adoption or renewal work is in flight** on that workspace — we don't surface a reminder on top of work that's already running.
- **Held when required state is missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting.** We don't render against uncertain inputs; the record stays held until the state is sound.

Both gates are evaluated fresh per display from the live ledger; nothing is reused, queued, or replayed off a prior display.

If the underlying need is to reach logged-in workspace members beyond qualifying admins (or any lifecycle email path), that is a separate program. It would need its own authorization, preflight, weekly-ceiling and audit controls, message-state controls, source-readiness check, fail-closed behavior, and rollback — none of which are in place, and I'm not opening that work from this thread.

Happy to talk through what the workspace-member problem actually is — there may be a path through CS-owned touch rather than the reminder — but the answer to "can we just show it to anyone logged in" is no.

— Riley

---

Draft is internal-tone, four-gate reaffirmation, fail-closed. I've also captured the scope decision in memory so the next Growth ping doesn't restart from zero. Nothing was sent externally — this is a draft for you to review and route.

CRITIQUE OF THE INES DRAFT

The exercise either needs to include the four-cell table or require learners to ask for it.

2. Effect size is the unadjusted headline. If learners see "7.3pp, p=.018" and nothing else, they will argue about whether 7.3pp is "big enough" rather than recognizing the unadjusted figure is the wrong number to ship on. 3. Stabilization is not a hard gate. First significance is not ship-ready. The draft needs to make stabilization-after-first-significance a non-negotiable step before any action, not a sentence buried in the conclusion.

4. Audience risk is missing. This 7.3 percentage-point difference is statistically significant (p = .018).

arguments.body:
# Helio Start — May continuation gate (draft)

Status: open. Continuation gate, NOT an expansion decision. This is the
evidence gate for May, not a Go signal for the bounded path itself.

## Frame

Two-decision structure, per Priya (2024-04-03):

1. Permission to **continue** the bounded Helio Start path is one decision.
2. Permission to **expand** it — eligibility widening, routed-before-setup
   relaxation, cohort-source broadening, paid acquisition, GA framing,
   forecastable pipeline, pricing-page exposure — is a separate decision and
   is explicitly out of scope. Continuing does not imply permission to expand.

Activation is one of five evidence lanes, not the headline. Widening,
launch, pipeline, and revenue language remain excluded.

## Cohort

Admitted Helio Start workspaces with complete day-7 windows only.

Kept out of every rate:

- Routed-before-setup cases.
- Ineligible cases.
- Assisted cases.
- Provisional / instrumentation-quality-only events.
- Day-7-incomplete rows.

Start stays separate from ordinary starter and retained mid-segment.
Activation stays separate from mature conversion, retention, revenue, and
forecastable pipeline.

## Continuation conditions (all must hold)

1. **Mature weekly cohort volume (PROPOSED — pending Priya's approval).**
   Hybrid threshold: at least three mature weekly cohorts of admitted
   Helio Start workspaces, **totaling at least 150 admitted accounts with
   complete day-7 windows**. The "three cohort" floor protects against
   reading a single large cohort as a trend; the "150 admitted-account"
   floor protects against three small cohorts reading as three lucky ones.
   Neither side of the conjunction stands on its own.

   Current reading against this proposed threshold: the first mature
   cohort (n=34 admitted / 23 activated = 67.6% / 12 support contacts
   across 9 workspaces, day-7 complete) contributes 34 of the proposed
   150-account floor, with two additional mature weekly cohorts still
   pending. The threshold is therefore **not yet met**, and a continuation
   decision is premature.

   This threshold is a **proposal**, not a decision. It is offered as a
   way to operationalize Priya's 2024-04-03 open question on whether
   "three cohorts" also needs a minimum mature-account count, and it
   awaits her approval before being treated as binding for May.

   Status flag: PROPOSED — pending Priya's approval. Marked here as the
   working hypothesis, not the agreed bar.

2. **Ordinary support coverage.** Support load stays within ordinary
   setup-question coverage plus ordinary permissions / ownership-review
   coverage. CS-routed contacts and pre-activation contacts stay
   measured separately. No new support tier is implicitly created by
   Start traffic.

3. **Zero crossings of published refusal boundaries.** Manual billing,
   CSV import, migration, unsupported permissions, unresolved ownership,
   agency-as-direct-admin, and provisional-as-confirmed cases all
   remain at zero admissions. Any single crossing is a gate failure
   regardless of how the other lanes read.

4. **Stable entitlement and lifecycle behavior.** Exactly one entitlement
   state and one support state per admitted workspace; entitlement /
   support-state guard stays clean; conservative non-state-changing
   lifecycle fork remains in place; ordinary-starter and retained
   mid-segment lifecycle behavior is unaffected.

5. **Exclusions hold.** Mature conversion, retention, revenue, and
   forecastable pipeline are explicitly **not** read out of this gate.
   Start is not a pipeline source, forecast input, or revenue-credit
   program during the bounded path.

## Five evidence lanes

Each lane has an owner, a definition, a current reading from the first
mature cohort (n=34 admitted, 23 activated = 67.6%, 12 contacts across
9 workspaces, day-7 complete), an envelope, and a gate-failure condition.

1. **Mature day-7 activation** — Owen (reporting). Definition: first
   supported integration within seven days, divided by all admitted
   workspaces with a complete day-7 window. Current reading: 23/34 =
   67.6% in the first mature cohort. Envelope: stable across three
   mature weekly cohorts under the proposed hybrid threshold
   (≥150 admitted accounts with complete day-7 windows, ≥3 cohorts);
   not a single-cohort trend read. Gate failure: instability across
   cohorts, or drift toward the ordinary-starter or retained
   mid-segment activation rates.
2. **Support load** — Owen with CS. Definition: ordinary setup questions
   plus permissions / ownership-review contacts per 100 admitted
   workspaces, including pre-activation contacts. Current reading:
   12 contacts / 9 workspaces across the first mature cohort.
   Envelope: stays within ordinary setup + ordinary permissions /
   ownership coverage. Gate failure: a contact pattern that requires
   new tooling, new staffing, or a new tier.
3. **Routing integrity** — Owen with CS. Definition: mutually exclusive
   final states (admitted / assisted / ineligible) with provisional /
   instrumentation-quality-only events held in a separate lane.
   Current reading: 64 = 34 admitted + 18 assisted + 12 ineligible,
   with the 4 provisional events kept out of activation, lifecycle, CS
   routing, support, and commercial metrics. Envelope: the
   reconciliation holds and no agency / manual-billing / import /
   migration case enters the admitted path. Gate failure: any
   reconciliation drift or any refusal-boundary crossing.
4. **Entitlement state** — Daniela. Definition: exactly one current
   entitlement state and one current support state per admitted
   workspace, with the entitlement / support-state guard keeping
   eligibility pending until both are current. Envelope: clean on new
   rows; historical `is_test` rows retained as legacy (no silent
   backfill). Gate failure: a duplicate or blank state, or any silent
   recoding.
5. **Lifecycle behavior** — Ines. Definition: conservative
   non-state-changing lifecycle fork only; routing rules for
   billing-mismatch / import-stuck / support-handoff remain
   education-only. Envelope: ordinary-starter and retained mid-segment
   templates untouched; lifecycle copy unchanged. Gate failure: a
   state-changing lifecycle edit, or any change that conflates Start
   with ordinary starter or retained mid-segment.

## What this gate does NOT decide

- Whether to widen eligibility.
- Whether to relax routed-before-setup rules.
- Whether to broaden cohort source.
- Whether to expose Start on the pricing page.
- Whether to run paid acquisition against Start.
- Whether to frame Start as a Q2 / Q3 / Q4 launch.
- Whether to take pipeline, forecast, or revenue credit for Start.

Any of those is a separate decision and is held until a continuation
decision is made on this gate's evidence.

## What changes if Priya approves the proposed hybrid threshold

- The continuation bar becomes: **at least three mature weekly cohorts,
  totaling at least 150 admitted accounts with complete day-7 windows**.
- "Three cohorts" alone is no longer sufficient (small cohorts could
  read as lucky).
- "150 admitted accounts" alone is no longer sufficient (could be one
  large cohort, not a stabilization read).
- The conjunction is the proposal; both floors are pending Priya's
  approval.

arguments.body:
# Helio Start — May continuation gate

## Frame (Priya, 2024-04-03)

This is a continuation-versus-expansion gate, not an expansion decision.

- **Permission to continue the bounded path is one decision.**
- **Permission to expand it — widening eligibility, relaxing routed-before-setup, broadening the cohort source, exposing paid acquisition, moving to GA framing, or treating results as forecastable pipeline — is a separate decision and is explicitly out of scope here.**
- Continuing the bounded path does not imply permission to expand it.

## Continuation conditions (all must hold)

Continuation into May is conditional on every item below. None of these is a forecast, pipeline, launch, GA, pricing-page-exposure, or paid-acquisition signal on its own or in aggregate.

1. **Three mature weekly cohorts.** At least three mature weekly cohorts of admitted Helio Start workspaces, each with a complete day-7 window. A single cohort — including the first mature cohort (n=34 admitted; 23 activated = 67.6%; 12 support contacts across 9 admitted workspaces) — is not a trend and not sufficient on its own.
2. **Ordinary support coverage.** Support load during the continuation window stays within ordinary setup-question coverage plus ordinary permissions/ownership-review coverage, consistent with the existing support-load envelope. No elevated support load is treated as a green light.
3. **Zero crossings of the published refusal boundaries.** Zero cases crossing the published refusal boundaries (manual billing, CSV import, migration, unsupported permissions, unresolved ownership, agency-as-direct-admin, or any other published refusal). Any single crossing fails the continuation condition, regardless of activation or support-load readings.
4. **Entitlement state, lifecycle behavior, and routing integrity** remain acceptable per the existing reporting, instrumentation, and routed-support lanes. No provisional eligibility event is treated as a confirmed admission; the four provisional events from the 3/19 export remain in the instrumentation-quality lane and stay excluded from activation, support, lifecycle, and commercial metrics.

## Mature-account floor — unresolved

The minimum mature-account count that "three mature weekly cohorts" should require is **unresolved**. Priya noted the three-cohort requirement without yet deciding whether it also needs a minimum mature-account floor. This brief does not pick a threshold. The continuation review will revisit this item if Priya sets one; until then, the three-cohort requirement is read as a cohort-count floor only, not an account-count floor.

## Forecast-language exclusion

- No "pipeline," "forecast," "revenue credit," "launch," "GA," "GA-ready," "pricing-page expansion," or "paid acquisition" language is used for this gate or its outcomes.
- The first-cohort 67.6% activation is descriptive evidence on one cohort. It is not a forecastable rate, not a launch number, not a revenue input, and not a basis for pricing-page or paid-acquisition exposure.
- Any continuation language that drifts toward forecast, pipeline, launch, GA, or revenue framing is out of scope for this brief and will be corrected before the May review.

## Cohort (kept unchanged from the earlier draft)

Admitted Helio Start workspaces with complete day-7 windows only. Routed-before-setup, ineligible, assisted, provisional/instrumentation-quality-only, and day-7-incomplete rows are kept out of every rate. Start stays separate from ordinary starter and retained mid-segment. Activation stays separate from mature conversion, retention, revenue, and forecastable pipeline.

## Refusal-boundary checks

The continuation review explicitly checks that no admitted workspace case has crossed any of the published refusal boundaries during the window. The check is zero-based: any single crossing fails the continuation condition. Checked conditions:

- Manual billing → assisted route-out, not admission.
- CSV import → assisted route-out, not admission.
- Migration → assisted route-out, not admission.
- Unsupported permissions → assisted route-out, not admission.
- Unresolved ownership → pending, no admission, no public path entry.
- Agency-as-direct-admin → assisted route-out, not admission; written client authorization is corroborating evidence for a handoff, not an override.
- Provisional eligibility events → retained in the instrumentation-quality lane only; never counted as admitted, never used in activation, support, lifecycle, or commercial metrics.

## Five evidence lanes (each with owner, definition, current reading, envelope, gate-failure condition)

Each lane is read on its own evidence. No lane is treated as a forecast, pipeline, or launch input. Lane separation is preserved.

1. **Mature day-7 activation** — Owen (reporting).
   - Definition: first integration within seven days, divided by all eligible starts in a mature weekly cohort. Nonactivating workspaces remain visible.
   - Current reading (first mature cohort only): n=34 admitted; 23 activated = 67.6%. One cohort; not a trend.
   - Envelope: stable within the existing under-50 simple-deployment band; no widening of eligibility or routed-before-setup rules.
   - Gate-failure condition: a mature-cohort activation rate that falls outside the existing envelope, OR a single cohort being read as a trend, OR activation being conflated with conversion, retention, revenue, or forecastable pipeline.

2. **Support load** — Owen with Customer Success.
   - Definition: ordinary setup questions plus permissions/ownership reviews per 100 eligible starts, including pre-activation contacts. Pre-setup routed contacts are reported separately from post-workspace support contacts.
   - Current reading (first mature cohort only): 12 support contacts across 9 admitted workspaces.
   - Envelope: ordinary setup coverage; no elevated load, no proxy-based Customer.io automation, no state-changing lifecycle branches.
   - Gate-failure condition: support load exceeds ordinary coverage, OR pre-setup routed contacts and post-workspace support contacts are merged, OR state-changing lifecycle branches are introduced on inferred/proxied state.

3. **Routing integrity** — Owen with Customer Success.
   - Definition: 64 = 34 admitted + 18 assisted + 12 ineligible (mutually exclusive final states); the 4 provisional eligibility events from 3/19 stay in the instrumentation-quality lane with both timestamps, final route-out reason, reviewer data, and a provisional-before-route-out flag; excluded from activation, lifecycle, CS routing, support, and commercial metrics.
   - Envelope: mutually exclusive final states, exact reconciliation to raw count, provisional events held separately.
   - Gate-failure condition: any admitted workspace crossing a published refusal boundary, any non-mutually-exclusive final state, any provisional event used as a confirmed admission, any raw-count/reported-count drift.

4. **Entitlement state** — Daniela.
   - Definition: entitlement/support-state guard keeps eligibility pending until both entitlement and support state are current; `integration_connected` requires `workspace_environment` ∈ {production, sandbox}; historical `admin_proof_attested` intact; prospective `verified_admin` derives from multiple conditions with ambiguous cases routed to CS.
   - Envelope: no entitlement/support-state drift; no proxy-based eligibility decisions; agency-domain cases stay routed out; blank support state stays `support_state_pending`.
   - Gate-failure condition: any entitlement/support-state drift, any proxy-based eligibility decision, any admitted workspace with a non-current entitlement or support state, any agency case admitted as a direct admin.

5. **Lifecycle behavior** — Ines.
   - Definition: conservative lifecycle fork; the safe beta path is two non-state-changing education touches (setup-checklist post-workspace-create, first-integration prep explainer) plus manual review; no proxy-based Customer.io automation for state-changing lifecycle branches; same-week confounders named in any renewal-readout language; ordinary starter path remains clearly separate.
   - Envelope: non-state-changing touches only; no commercial Expansion Assist framing; no Helio Start lifecycle change treated as a Q4 launch/pipeline/forecast/revenue/day-60 replacement.
   - Gate-failure condition: any state-changing lifecycle branch on inferred/proxied state, any renewal reminder interpreted as a commercial Expansion Assist prompt while CS adoption work is open, any expansion-nudge learning being read as a Helio Start proof point.

## Expansion Assist, ordinary starter, retained mid-segment — kept separate

- Expansion Assist remains Q4 shadow-review design work; it has not yet produced an output and is not a Helio Start lane.
- The ordinary starter path remains clearly separate from Helio Start. Activation-definition-v3 on ordinary starter trials is not merged into Start reporting.
- Retained mid-segment (75–200 v2, 50–75 band) remains separate from Start. The 118-seat Acme Dev Shop renewal scenario stays out of Start reporting and out of any Start continuation read.

## What the May continuation review will and will not decide

- **Will decide:** whether the bounded path continues, holds, or pauses, based on the five lanes above, the three-cohort requirement, ordinary support coverage, and zero refusal-boundary crossings.
- **Will not decide:** eligibility widening, routed-before-setup relaxation, broader-beta widening, pricing-page exposure, paid acquisition, GA framing, pipeline framing, forecast framing, or revenue credit. Those are separate decisions, none of which are implied by continuing the bounded path.

## Open items

- **Mature-account floor (unresolved).** Priya has not yet decided whether "three mature weekly cohorts" requires a minimum mature-account count. This brief does not pick a threshold. The May review will treat the three-cohort requirement as a cohort-count floor only unless and until Priya sets an account-count floor.
- First-cohort descriptive readings remain one-cohort evidence; no second or third mature weekly cohort has been read yet for this gate.

messages.content: [2024-01-22T13:45:00-06:00] Customer Success turned the completed renewal analysis into a draft collaborator-invite reminder experiment, and it overreaches. It jumps from an observed association to an eight-point causal hypothesis without controlling for current reminder exposure, adoption-plan state, or varying time to renewal. It also wants to stop at the first p-value below .05 and doesn't name any support-load or unsubscribe guardrails. Please assess it under our Q1 investigation framework, call out the causal and measurement defects, and rewrite it as the smallest defensible design with an explicit denominator, exposure, observation window, effect-size bar, stabilization requirement, support-load guardrails, and lifecycle-risk guardrails. If the available population and horizon can't actually support that, say not to run it.

VERDICT
Don't run as drafted. Same trap as the Q4 active-admin case (7.3 raw → 2.4 adjusted, CI [-1.8, +6.6], trigger removed). Rewrite as the smallest defensible design below; if the post-filter eligible subset can't support two cohorts plus a full renewal-cycle observation, keep recent-invite behavior as descriptive / CS watchlist input only. Do not ship.

DEFECTS IN THE CS DRAFT

Causal overreach
- Association vs. causation. The 11.8-point descriptive gap (54/65 vs. 139/195, 83.1% vs. 71.3%) describes healthier accounts. Accounts that invite collaborators are very likely more engaged regardless of any reminder — invites probably describe health, they don't drive renewal. This is structurally the Q4 active-admin pattern.
- Eight-point causal hypothesis with no isolation. Bundling current-reminder exposure, adoption-plan state, and time-to-renewal heterogeneity into one test means any observed effect is uninterpretable — you can't tell which lever moved, or whether none did.
- Confounders the draft does not control:
  - Current reminder exposure (existing lifecycle stream gives different baseline cadences to different accounts)
  - Open CS adoption plans (these accounts are mid-onboarding; renewal dynamics aren't comparable)
  - Varying time to renewal (7 days out vs. 90 days out have different baseline probabilities)
  - Reverse causation risk (a renewal-approaching account may invite a teammate under internal pressure, not the reminder)
- Unobserved account-level variation (workspace size, integration depth, admin tenure, single vs. multi-admin) almost certainly correlates with both invite likelihood and renewal.

Measurement overreach
- First p<.05 is not the bar. The Q4 active-admin case shipped a 7.3-point raw effect with p=.018; after adjustment it collapsed to 2.4 points with a CI crossing zero and the trigger was removed. First significance without adjustment is a known false-positive pathway.
- 52 of 312 eligible accounts are unclassified. Treating the 260 classified as the population without naming that gap invites silent selection bias.
- No effect-size bar. A noisy estimate crossing .05 is not the same as a meaningful lift.
- No support-load or unsubscribe guardrails. A reminder sent into in-flight CS work, recent support contacts, or commercial conversations is a known risk path, not theoretical.

SMALLEST DEFENSIBLE DESIGN

Cohort and denominator (Owen owns)
- Single index event. Anchor on day 10 of trial for forward-going cohorts (or a fixed-time-to-renewal cohort for retrospective) so every account enters the test in the same state.
- Pre-specified eligibility filters:
  - Zero collaborator invites as of index
  - No open CS adoption plan
  - No support contact in prior 14 days
  - Single primary admin (or cleanly attributable admin set)
  - Renewal date 30-90 days out at index (uniform horizon)
  - Either not in any other reminder stream, or that stream held constant across treatment and control
- Show: eligible / excluded by reason / final action audience, with the 52 unclassified bucket named and either reclassified or carried as an explicit exclusion reason.
- Account-level state must be clean before assignment: no duplicate workspaces, no ambiguous admin.

Exposure
- One additional reminder, sent within a defined window after index (e.g., day 11-12).
- 50/50 random assignment at the account level within cohort. Document copy, send time, suppression set, and the unchanged state of all other reminder streams during the test window.
- Treatment gets the reminder; control does not. No within-account crossover.

Observation window
- Primary outcome: invite uptake within 7-14 days post-send.
- Secondary outcome: renewal, observed only after the cohort passes its full renewal date. No "reminder works on renewal" claim before the full cycle closes.
- Stabilization cohort: a second independent cohort, same design, same denominators, run after the first cohort's primary outcome is in hand.
